extraction_notes.comment: Level-by-level class progression. Each class carries core_traits, a progression_table (per-level resource columns), and features_by_level nodes 1-20. Each feature node carries verbatim text and, where it grants a build choice, an interaction_type (nested_subchoice_tree for subclass/ASI/option picks, proficiency_allocation_matrix for skill picks, derived_value_multiplier for flat stat changes) plus a choices[] array. Subclasses are nested in each class's subclasses[] array, each with its own source_book tag and features_by_level. BUILD STATUS: this file is assembled class-by-class across multiple extraction passes; see build_progress.

1.name: Rage
1.text: You can imbue yourself with a primal power called Rage, a force that grants you extraordinary might and resilience. You can enter your Rage as a Bonus Action. You can enter your Rage the number of times shown for your Barbarian level in the Rages column of the Barbarian Features table. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. While active, your Rage follows these rules: Damage Resistance - you have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage. Rage Damage - when you make an attack using Strength and deal damage, you gain a bonus to the damage shown in the Rage Damage column. Strength Advantage - you have Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. No Concentration or Spells - you can't maintain Concentration and can't cast spells. Duration - the Rage lasts until the end of your next turn and ends early if you don Heavy armor or have the Incapacitated condition; extend it each round by attacking an enemy, forcing a save, or taking a Bonus Action. Maximum 10 minutes.

choices.label: Rage uses (tracked resource; see progression_table Rages column)

actions.name: Rage
actions.effect: Enter Rage: damage resistance to B/P/S, Rage Damage bonus, Advantage on STR checks/saves

1.description: You can imbue yourself with a primal power called Rage, a force that grants you extraordinary might and resilience. You can enter it as a Bonus Action if you aren't wearing Heavy armor. While raging, you gain the following benefits: Damage Resistance (Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing), Rage Damage (+2 bonus to Strength-based damage rolls, increasing at higher levels), Strength Advantage (Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws). The Rage lasts until the end of your next turn unless you use a Bonus Action to extend it, or until you have the Incapacitated condition or don Heavy armor. You can Rage a number of times shown in the Rages column of the Barbarian table.

1.name: Unarmored Defense
1.text: While you aren't wearing any armor, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Constitution modifiers. You can use a Shield and still gain this benefit.
1.description: While you aren't wearing any armor, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity modifier plus your Constitution modifier. You can use a Shield and still gain this benefit.

1.name: Weapon Mastery
1.text: Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of Simple or Martial Melee weapons of your choice, such as Greataxes and Handaxes. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices. When you reach certain Barbarian levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Barbarian Features table.

choices.label: Weapon Mastery weapons (count scales: 2 at L1, 3 at L4, 4 at L10)

1.description: Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of simple or martial melee weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose.

2.name: Danger Sense
2.text: You gain an uncanny sense of when things aren't as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge perils. You have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws unless you have the Incapacitated condition.
2.description: You gain an uncanny sense of when things nearby aren't as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge out of the way. You have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws unless you have the Incapacitated condition.

2.name: Reckless Attack
2.text: You can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with increased ferocity. When you make your first attack roll on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you Advantage on attack rolls using Strength until the start of your next turn, but attack rolls against you have Advantage during that time.
2.description: You can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack roll on your turn using a Strength-based attack, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you Advantage on attack rolls using Strength until the start of your next turn, but attack rolls against you have Advantage during that time.

3.name: Barbarian Subclass
3.text: You gain a Barbarian subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Barbarian levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Barbarian level or lower.
3.description: You gain a Barbarian subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Barbarian levels.

3.name: Primal Knowledge
3.text: You gain proficiency in another skill of your choice from the skill list available to Barbarians at level 1. In addition, while your Rage is active, you can channel primal power when you attempt certain tasks; whenever you make an ability check using Acrobatics, Intimidation, Perception, Stealth, or Survival, you can make it as a Strength check even if it normally uses a different ability.
3.description: You gain proficiency in another skill of your choice from the skills available to Barbarians at character creation. In addition, while your Rage is active, you can channel primal power when you attempt certain tasks; whenever you make an ability check using one of the following skills, you can make it as a Strength check that also benefits from your Rage: Acrobatics, Intimidation, Perception, Stealth, or Survival.

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
4.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Barbarian levels 8, 12, and 16.
4.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Barbarian levels 8, 12, 16, and 19.

5.name: Extra Attack
5.text: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
5.description: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

5.name: Fast Movement

7.name: Instinctive Pounce
7.text: As part of the Bonus Action you take to enter your Rage, you can move up to half your Speed.

9.name: Brutal Strike
9.text: If you use Reckless Attack, you can forgo any Advantage on one Strength-based attack roll of your choice on your turn. The chosen attack roll mustn't have Disadvantage. If the chosen attack roll hits, the target takes an extra 1d10 damage of the same type dealt by the weapon or Unarmed Strike, and you can cause one Brutal Strike effect of your choice. Forceful Blow: the target is pushed 15 feet straight away from you, and you can then move up to half your Speed straight toward it without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Hamstring Blow: the target's Speed is reduced by 15 feet until the start of your next turn (only one Hamstring Blow at a time).
9.description: If you use Reckless Attack, you can forgo any Advantage on one Strength-based attack roll of your choice on your turn. The chosen attack roll mustn't have Disadvantage. If the chosen attack roll hits, the target takes an extra 1d10 damage of the same type dealt by the weapon or Unarmed Strike, and you can impose one of the following Brutal Strike effects: Forceful Blow (push the target up to 15 ft straight away from you) or Hamstring Blow (reduce the target's Speed by 15 ft until the start of your next turn). At level 13 you gain two additional effects and deal an extra 2d10. At level 17, extra damage increases to 3d10.

10.description: You gain a feature from your Barbarian subclass.

11.name: Relentless Rage
11.text: Your Rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 Hit Points while your Rage is active and don't die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, your Hit Points instead change to a number equal to twice your Barbarian level. Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a Short or Long Rest, the DC resets to 10.
11.description: Your Rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 Hit Points while your Rage is active and don't die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. 13.name: Improved Brutal Strike
13.text: You have honed new ways to attack furiously. The following effects are now among your Brutal Strike options. Staggering Blow: the target has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes, and it can't make Opportunity Attacks until the start of your next turn. Sundering Blow: before the start of your next turn, the next attack roll made by another creature against the target gains a +5 bonus to the roll (an attack roll can gain only one Sundering Blow bonus).
13.description: You now have two additional Brutal Strike effects to choose from when you use that feature: Staggering Blow (the target has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn) and Sundering Blow (before the start of your next turn, the next attack roll made by a creature other than you against the target gains a +5 bonus to the roll). Additionally, the extra damage increases to 2d10.

15.name: Persistent Rage
15.text: When you roll Initiative, you can regain all expended uses of Rage. After you regain uses of Rage in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest. In addition, your Rage is so fierce that it now lasts for 10 minutes without you needing to do anything to extend it from round to round. Your Rage ends early if you have the Unconscious condition (not just the Incapacitated condition) or don Heavy armor.
15.description: When you roll Initiative, you can regain all expended uses of Rage. After you benefit from this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

18.name: Indomitable Might
18.text: If your total for a Strength check or Strength saving throw is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.
18.description: If your total for a Strength check or Strength saving throw is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.

19.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Irresistible Offense is recommended.
19.description: You gain the Epic Boon of Irresistible Offense or another Epic Boon feat of your choice.

20.name: Primal Champion
20.text: You embody primal power. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.
20.description: You embody primal power. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

subclasses.name: Path of the Berserker
subclasses.tagline: Channel Rage into Violent Fury
subclasses.description: Barbarians who walk the Path of the Berserker direct their Rage primarily toward violence. Their path is one of untrammeled fury, and they thrill in the chaos of battle as they allow their Rage to seize and empower them.

3.name: Frenzy
3.text: If you use Reckless Attack while your Rage is active, you deal extra damage to the first target you hit on your turn with a Strength-based attack. To determine the extra damage, roll a number of d6s equal to your Rage Damage bonus, and add them together. The damage has the same type as the weapon or Unarmed Strike used for the attack.

6.name: Mindless Rage
6.text: You have Immunity to the Charmed and Frightened conditions while your Rage is active. If you're Charmed or Frightened when you enter your Rage, the condition ends on you.

10.name: Retaliation
10.text: When you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can take a Reaction to make one melee attack against that creature, using a weapon or an Unarmed Strike.

actions.name: Retaliation
actions.casting_time: Reaction (when damaged by a creature within 5 ft)
actions.effect: Make one melee attack against that creature

14.name: Intimidating Presence
14.text: As a Bonus Action, you can strike terror into others with your menacing presence and primal power. Each creature of your choice in a 30-foot Emanation originating from you must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, a creature has the Frightened condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of the Frightened creature's turns, the creature repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest unless you expend a use of your Rage (no action required) to restore your use of it.

actions.name: Intimidating Presence
actions.effect: WIS save (DC 8 + STR + Prof) or Frightened 1 min

features.name: Frenzy
features.description: When you rage, you can go into a frenzy. For the duration of your rage you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after this one. When your rage ends, you suffer one level of exhaustion.

features.name: Mindless Rage
features.description: You can't be charmed or frightened while raging. If you are charmed or frightened when you enter your rage, the effect is suspended for the duration of the rage.

features.name: Retaliation
features.description: When you take damage from a creature within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature.

features.name: Intimidating Presence
features.description: As an action, choose one creature within 30 feet that can see or hear you. It must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns you can use your action to extend this effect. The effect ends if the target ends its turn out of line of sight or more than 60 feet away.

subclasses.name: Path of the Wild Heart
subclasses.tagline: Walk in Community with the Animal World
subclasses.description: Barbarians who follow the Path of the Wild Heart view themselves as kin to animals. These Barbarians learn magical means to communicate with animals, and their Rage heightens their connection to animals as it fills them with supernatural might.

3.name: Animal Speaker
3.text: You can cast the Beast Sense and Speak with Animals spells but only as Rituals. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for them.

spells.name: Beast Sense
spells.effect: See and hear through a willing Beast's senses.

spells.name: Speak with Animals
spells.effect: Comprehend and verbally communicate with Beasts.

3.name: Rage of the Wilds
3.text: Your Rage taps into the primal power of animals. Whenever you activate your Rage, you gain one of the following options of your choice.

choices.label: Rage of the Wilds option (choose each time you Rage)

options.name: Bear
options.text: While your Rage is active, you have Resistance to every damage type except Force, Necrotic, Psychic, and Radiant.

options.name: Eagle
options.text: When you activate your Rage, you can take the Disengage and Dash actions as part of that Bonus Action. While your Rage is active, you can take a Bonus Action to take both of those actions.

options.name: Wolf
options.text: While your Rage is active, your allies have Advantage on attack rolls against any enemy of yours within 5 feet of you.

6.name: Aspect of the Wilds
6.text: You gain one of the following options of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your choice.

choices.label: Aspect of the Wilds (swappable on Long Rest)

options.name: Owl
options.text: You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet. If you already have Darkvision, its range increases by 60 feet.

options.name: Panther
options.text: You have a Climb Speed equal to your Speed.

options.name: Salmon
options.text: You have a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.

10.name: Nature Speaker
10.text: You can cast the Commune with Nature spell but only as a Ritual. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it.

spells.name: Commune with Nature
spells.effect: Gain knowledge of the surrounding territory (3 miles outdoors / 300 ft underground).

14.name: Power of the Wilds
14.text: Whenever you activate your Rage, you gain one of the following options of your choice.

choices.label: Power of the Wilds option (choose each time you Rage)

options.name: Falcon
options.text: While your Rage is active, you have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed if you aren't wearing any armor.

options.name: Lion
options.text: While your Rage is active, any of your enemies within 5 feet of you have Disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you or another Barbarian who has this option active.

options.name: Ram
options.text: While your Rage is active, you can cause a Large or smaller creature to have the Prone condition when you hit it with a melee attack.

features.name: Animal Speaker
features.description: You can cast Beast Sense and Speak with Animals as rituals. You can also cast these spells normally, expending a spell slot if you have one.

features.name: Rage of the Wilds
features.description: Your rage taps into the primal nature of animals. You gain one of the following options of your choice, and you can change your choice whenever you gain a Barbarian level: Bear (resistance to all damage except Force and Psychic while raging), Eagle (you can use Dash as a bonus action while raging), Elk (your speed increases by 15 feet while raging), Wolf (your allies have advantage on attack rolls against enemies within 5 feet of you while you rage).

features.name: Aspect of the Wilds
features.description: You gain one of the following options of your choice, and you can change your choice whenever you gain a Barbarian level: Bear (advantage on Strength checks, carrying capacity doubled), Eagle (you can see up to 1 mile clearly), Elk (your travel pace and that of companions doubles), Wolf (you can track at a fast pace and move stealthily at a normal pace).

features.name: Nature Speaker
features.description: You can cast Commune with Nature as a ritual.

features.name: Power of the Wilds
features.description: You gain one of the following options of your choice, and you can change your choice whenever you gain a Barbarian level: Bear (hostile creatures within 5 feet have disadvantage on attacks against targets other than you), Eagle (you gain a Fly Speed equal to your Speed while raging), Wolf (you can knock a Large or smaller creature Prone when you hit it with an attack while raging, as a bonus action).

subclasses.name: Path of the World Tree
subclasses.tagline: Trace the Roots and Branches of the Multiverse
subclasses.description: Barbarians who follow the Path of the World Tree connect with the cosmic tree Yggdrasil through their Rage. This tree grows among the Outer Planes, connecting them to each other and the Material Plane. These Barbarians draw on the tree's magic for vitality and as a means of dimensional travel.

3.name: Vitality of the Tree
3.text: Your Rage taps into the life force of the World Tree. Vitality Surge: when you activate your Rage, you gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to your Barbarian level. Life-Giving Force: at the start of each of your turns while your Rage is active, you can choose another creature within 10 feet of yourself to gain Temporary Hit Points; roll a number of d6s equal to your Rage Damage bonus and add them together. If any of these Temporary Hit Points remain when your Rage ends, they vanish.

6.name: Branches of the Tree
6.text: Whenever a creature you can see starts its turn within 30 feet of you while your Rage is active, you can take a Reaction to summon spectral branches of the World Tree around it. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or be teleported to an unoccupied space you can see within 5 feet of yourself or in the nearest unoccupied space you can see. After the target teleports, you can reduce its Speed to 0 until the end of the current turn.

actions.name: Branches of the Tree
actions.effect: STR save or teleport target adjacent to you; may reduce its Speed to 0

10.name: Battering Roots
10.text: During your turn, your reach is 10 feet greater with any Melee weapon that has the Heavy or Versatile property, as tendrils of the World Tree extend from you. When you hit with such a weapon on your turn, you can activate the Push or Topple mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you're using with that weapon.

14.name: Travel Along the Tree
14.text: When you activate your Rage and as a Bonus Action while your Rage is active, you can teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. In addition, once per Rage, you can increase the range of that teleport to 150 feet; when you do so, you can also bring up to six willing creatures who are within 10 feet of you. Each creature teleports to an unoccupied space of your choice within 10 feet of your destination space.

actions.name: Travel Along the Tree
actions.effect: Teleport to an unoccupied space you can see

features.name: Vitality of the Tree
features.description: Your Rage taps into the life force of the World Tree. You gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Barbarian level when you enter your Rage. At the start of each of your turns while raging, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Rage Damage bonus.

features.name: Branches of the Tree
features.description: While raging, you can use a bonus action to magically teleport. You vanish and reappear within 60 feet in an unoccupied space you can see. If you teleport next to a creature, you can force it to make a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier). On a failed save, you move the creature to an unoccupied space within 30 feet of you.

features.name: Battering Roots
features.description: During your Rage, your reach increases by 10 feet. When you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can activate the Shove option on the attack without using a bonus action.

features.name: Travel Along the Tree
features.description: When you activate your Rage and at the start of each of your turns while it lasts, you can teleport one willing creature within 5 feet of you to any unoccupied space you can see within 500 feet of you. Once per Rage you can use this feature to teleport up to six willing creatures within 10 feet of you up to 500 feet.

subclasses.name: Path of the Zealot
subclasses.tagline: Rage in Ecstatic Union with a God
subclasses.description: Barbarians who walk the Path of the Zealot receive boons from a god or pantheon. These Barbarians experience their Rage as an ecstatic episode of divine union that infuses them with power. They are often allies to the priests and other followers of their god or pantheon.

3.name: Divine Fury
3.text: You can channel divine power into your strikes. On each of your turns while your Rage is active, the first creature you hit with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike takes extra damage equal to 1d6 plus half your Barbarian level (round down). The extra damage is Necrotic or Radiant; you choose the type each time you deal the damage.

3.name: Warrior of the Gods
3.text: A divine entity helps ensure you can continue the fight. You have a pool of four d12s that you can spend to heal yourself. As a Bonus Action, you can expend dice from the pool, roll them, and regain a number of Hit Points equal to the roll's total. Your pool regains all expended dice when you finish a Long Rest. The pool's maximum number of dice increases by one when you reach Barbarian levels 6 (5 dice), 12 (6 dice), and 17 (7 dice).

actions.name: Warrior of the Gods
actions.effect: Expend d12s from the pool; regain HP equal to the total
actions.uses_note: Pool: 4 d12 (5 at L6, 6 at L12, 7 at L17)

6.name: Fanatical Focus
6.text: Once per active Rage, if you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it with a bonus equal to your Rage Damage bonus, and you must use the new roll.

10.name: Zealous Presence
10.text: As a Bonus Action, you unleash a battle cry infused with divine energy. Up to ten other creatures of your choice within 60 feet of you gain Advantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the start of your next turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest unless you expend a use of your Rage (no action required) to restore your use of it.

actions.name: Zealous Presence
actions.effect: Up to 10 allies gain Advantage on attacks and saves until start of your next turn

14.name: Rage of the Gods
14.text: When you activate your Rage, you can assume the form of a divine warrior. This form lasts for 1 minute or until you drop to 0 Hit Points. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest. While in this form: Flight - you have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed and can hover. Resistance - you have Resistance to Necrotic, Psychic, and Radiant damage. Revivification - when a creature within 30 feet of you would drop to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to expend a use of your Rage to instead change the target's Hit Points to a number equal to your Barbarian level.

actions.name: Rage of the Gods
actions.effect: Divine warrior form for 1 min: Fly Speed, Resistance to Necrotic/Psychic/Radiant, Revivification

features.name: Divine Fury
features.description: While raging, the first creature you hit on each turn with a weapon attack takes extra damage equal to 1d6 + half your Barbarian level. The extra damage is Necrotic or Radiant (your choice when you gain this feature).

features.name: Warrior of the Gods
features.description: A divine entity helps ensure you can continue to fight. You have a pool of four d12s. When a creature would cast a spell to restore your Hit Points, that creature can expend dice from this pool instead of spending a spell slot. The restored hit points equal the dice roll plus the caster's spellcasting ability modifier. You regain all expended dice when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Fanatical Focus
features.description: Once per Rage, if you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it and must use the new roll.

features.name: Zealous Presence
features.description: As a Bonus Action, you unleash a battle cry. Up to ten creatures of your choice within 60 feet that can hear you gain advantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the start of your next turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest unless you expend a use of your Rage to use it again.

features.name: Rage Beyond Death
features.description: While raging, having 0 Hit Points doesn't knock you Unconscious. You still must make Death Saving Throws, and you die if you accumulate three failures. If your Rage is still active when you are stabilized, your Rage ends. Your Rage ends early if you end your turn with 0 Hit Points and are not making Death Saving Throws.

subclasses.name: Path of the Ancestral Guardian
subclasses.edition_note: Originally published for 2014 rules in Xanathar's Guide to Everything; feature levels are as printed in that book.
subclasses.tagline: Call on Guardian Spirits of Your Ancestors
subclasses.description: Some barbarians hail from cultures that revere their ancestors. These tribes teach that the warriors of the past linger in the world as mighty spirits, who can guide and protect the living. When a barbarian who follows this path rages, the barbarian contacts the spirit world and calls on these guardian spirits for aid.

3.name: Ancestral Protectors
3.text: Spectral warriors appear when you enter your rage. While you're raging, the first creature you hit with an attack on your turn becomes the target of the warriors, which hinder its attacks. Until the start of your next turn, that target has disadvantage on any attack roll that isn't against you, and when the target hits a creature other than you with an attack, that creature has resistance to the damage dealt by the attack. The effect on the target ends early if your rage ends.

6.name: Spirit Shield
6.text: The guardian spirits that aid you can provide supernatural protection to those you defend. If you are raging and another creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to reduce that damage by 2d6. When you reach certain levels in this class, you can reduce the damage by more: by 3d6 at 10th level and by 4d6 at 14th level.

actions.name: Spirit Shield
actions.effect: Reduce damage to a creature by 2d6 (3d6 at 10th, 4d6 at 14th)

10.name: Consult the Spirits
10.text: You gain the ability to consult with your ancestral spirits. When you do so, you cast the Augury or Clairvoyance spell, without using a spell slot or material components. Rather than creating a spherical sensor, this use of Clairvoyance invisibly summons one of your ancestral spirits to the chosen location. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells. After you cast either spell in this way, you can't use this feature again until you finish a short or long rest.

14.name: Vengeful Ancestors
14.text: Your ancestral spirits grow powerful enough to retaliate. When you use your Spirit Shield to reduce the damage of an attack, the attacker takes an amount of force damage equal to the damage that your Spirit Shield prevents.

features.name: Ancestral Protectors
features.description: While raging, the first creature you hit each turn becomes marked by ancestral spirits. Until the start of your next turn, the marked target has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you, and any creature other than you that the marked target hits with an attack gains resistance to that damage.

features.name: Spirit Shield
features.description: While raging, if a creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage, you can use your reaction to reduce that damage by 2d6. This increases to 3d6 at 10th level and 4d6 at 14th level.

features.name: Consult the Spirits
features.description: You can cast Augury or Clairvoyance without a spell slot or material components. Rather than a sensor, Clairvoyance summons an ancestral spirit. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining uses on a Long Rest.

features.name: Vengeful Ancestors
features.description: When you use Spirit Shield to reduce damage, the attacker takes force damage equal to the amount reduced.

subclasses.name: Path of the Storm Herald
subclasses.edition_note: Originally published for 2014 rules in Xanathar's Guide to Everything; feature levels are as printed in that book.
subclasses.tagline: Transform Your Rage into a Mantle of Primal Magic
subclasses.description: Barbarians who follow the Path of the Storm Herald learn to transform their rage into a mantle of primal magic that swirls around them. When in a fury, a barbarian of this path taps into the forces of nature to create powerful magical effects.

3.name: Storm Aura
3.text: You emanate a stormy, magical aura while you rage. The aura extends 10 feet from you in every direction, but not through total cover. Your aura has an effect that activates when you enter your rage, and you can activate the effect again on each of your turns as a bonus action. Choose desert, sea, or tundra; your aura's effect depends on that chosen environment, and you can change your choice whenever you gain a level in this class. If your aura's effects require a saving throw, the DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier. Desert: When this effect is activated, all other creatures in your aura take 2 fire damage each (increasing to 3 at 5th level, 4 at 10th, 5 at 15th, and 6 at 20th). Sea: When activated, you can choose one other creature you can see in your aura; the target must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 1d6 lightning damage on a failed save or half as much on a success (increasing to 2d6 at 10th level, 3d6 at 15th, and 4d6 at 20th). Tundra: When activated, each creature of your choice in your aura gains 2 temporary hit points (increasing to 3 at 5th level, 4 at 10th, 5 at 15th, and 6 at 20th).

actions.name: Storm Aura
actions.effect: Activate your Storm Aura's environment effect

6.name: Storm Soul
6.text: The storm grants you benefits even when your aura isn't active, based on the environment you chose for your Storm Aura. Desert: You gain resistance to fire damage, and you don't suffer the effects of extreme heat; as an action, you can touch a flammable object that isn't being worn or carried by anyone else and set it on fire. Sea: You gain resistance to lightning damage, you can breathe underwater, and you gain a swimming speed of 30 feet. Tundra: You gain resistance to cold damage, and you don't suffer the effects of extreme cold; as an action, you can touch water and turn a 5-foot cube of it into ice, which melts after 1 minute (this fails if a creature is in the cube).

10.name: Shielding Storm
10.text: You learn to use your mastery of the storm to protect others. Each creature of your choice has the damage resistance you gained from the Storm Soul feature while the creature is in your Storm Aura.

14.name: Raging Storm
14.text: The power of the storm you channel grows mightier, lashing out at your foes. The effect is based on the environment you chose for your Storm Aura. Desert: Immediately after a creature in your aura hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to force that creature to make a Dexterity saving throw; on a failed save, the creature takes fire damage equal to half your barbarian level. Sea: When you hit a creature in your aura with an attack, you can use your reaction to force that creature to make a Strength saving throw; on a failed save, the creature is knocked prone, as if struck by a wave. Tundra: Whenever the effect of your Storm Aura is activated, you can choose one creature you can see in the aura; that creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw, or its speed is reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn, as magical frost covers it.

features.name: Storm Aura
features.description: While raging, you emanate a stormy aura in a 10-foot radius. When you enter your rage and as a bonus action on your turns, you can activate one of these effects: Desert (each creature of your choice in the aura takes 1d6 fire damage, increasing at higher levels), Sea (one target makes a Dexterity save or takes 1d6 lightning damage, increasing at higher levels), Tundra (creatures of your choice gain 2 temporary HP, increasing at higher levels).

features.name: Storm Soul
features.description: You gain benefits based on your chosen environment: Desert (resistance to fire damage, immune to extreme heat), Sea (resistance to lightning damage, can breathe underwater), Tundra (resistance to cold damage, immune to extreme cold).

features.name: Shielding Storm
features.description: Creatures of your choice in your Storm Aura gain the damage resistance from your Storm Soul feature.

features.name: Raging Storm
features.description: Your storm's power intensifies: Desert (reaction after being hit — target makes Dex save or takes fire damage equal to half your level), Sea (after hitting a target in your aura, use reaction to knock it Prone on a failed Strength save), Tundra (when Storm Aura activates, one creature makes a Strength save or its speed is reduced to 0 until your next turn).

features.name: Magic Awareness
features.description: As an action, you can open your awareness to the presence of concentrated magic. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any spell or magic item within 60 feet of you that isn't behind total cover. When you sense a spell, you know which school of magic it belongs to. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Wild Surge
features.description: The magic that suffuses you causes you to unleash bursts of wild magic. Whenever you enter your Rage, roll on the Wild Magic Surge table (d8). The wild magic effects include: puffs of colored smoke, damage reduction, magical bolts, spectral shield, speedy recovery, teleport, temporary fly speed, or retributive psychic damage. The effect lasts until your Rage ends.

features.name: Bolstering Magic
features.description: You can harness wild magic to bolster yourself or a companion. As an action, you can touch one creature (which can be yourself) and confer one of the following benefits of your choice to that creature: For 10 minutes, the creature can roll a d3 whenever it makes an attack roll or an ability check and add the number rolled to the result; or Roll a d3. The creature regains one expended spell slot of a level equal to or lower than the number rolled.

features.name: Unstable Backlash
features.description: When you are imperiled during your Rage, the magic within you can lash out; immediately after you take damage or fail a saving throw while raging, you can use your Reaction to roll on the Wild Magic Surge table and immediately produce the effect rolled.

features.name: Controlled Surge
features.description: Whenever you roll on the Wild Magic Surge table, you can roll the die twice and choose which of the two effects to unleash. If you roll the same number on both dice, you can ignore the number and choose any effect on the table.

options.name: Option A
options.text: Leather Armor, 2 Daggers, Musical Instrument of your choice, Entertainer's Pack, and 19 GP

options.name: Option B
options.text: 90 GP

1.name: Bardic Inspiration
1.text: You can supernaturally inspire others through words, music, or dance. This inspiration is represented by your Bardic Inspiration die, which is a d6 (it becomes a d8 at level 5, a d10 at level 10, and a d12 at level 15). As a Bonus Action, you can inspire another creature within 60 feet of yourself who can see or hear you; that creature gains one of your Bardic Inspiration dice. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time. Once within the next hour when the creature fails a D20 Test, it can roll the die and add the number rolled to the d20, potentially turning the failure into a success. You can confer a Bardic Inspiration die a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

actions.name: Bardic Inspiration
actions.effect: Give a creature a Bardic Inspiration die (d6/d8/d10/d12 by level)

1.description: You can supernaturally inspire others through words, music, or dance. As a Bonus Action, you can inspire one creature you can see or hear within 60 feet. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die (a d6). Once within the next hour, the creature can roll that die and add the number rolled to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. The creature can wait until after it rolls the d20 before deciding to use the Bardic Inspiration die, but must decide before the DM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. The die size increases at higher Bard levels (d8 at level 5, d10 at level 10, d12 at level 15). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

1.name: Spellcasting
1.text: You have learned to cast spells through your bardic arts. Cantrips: you know two cantrips of your choice from the Bard spell list (Dancing Lights and Vicious Mockery recommended); you learn another at levels 4 and 10. Spell Slots: the Bard Features table shows how many spell slots you have; you regain all expended slots on a Long Rest. Prepared Spells of Level 1+: you prepare a list of level 1+ Bard spells, starting with four level 1 spells; the number increases as you gain levels. Charisma is your spellcasting ability. You can use a Musical Instrument as a Spellcasting Focus.

choices.label: Prepared Spells (from Bard list; count per progression_table)

1.description: You have learned to untangle and reshape the fabric of reality in harmony with your wishes and music. Charisma is your spellcasting ability.

2.name: Expertise
2.text: You gain Expertise in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. Performance and Persuasion are recommended if you have proficiency in them. At Bard level 9, you gain Expertise in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.
2.description: You gain Expertise in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

2.name: Jack of All Trades
2.text: You can add half your Proficiency Bonus (round down) to any ability check you make that uses a skill proficiency you lack and that doesn't otherwise use your Proficiency Bonus.
2.description: You can add half your Proficiency Bonus (rounded down) to any ability check you make that uses a skill proficiency you lack, provided the check isn't already benefiting from your Proficiency Bonus.

3.name: Bard Subclass
3.text: You gain a Bard subclass of your choice. The College of Dance, College of Glamour, College of Lore, and College of Valor subclasses are detailed in this class's subclasses array. A subclass grants you features at certain Bard levels.
3.description: You gain a Bard subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Bard levels.

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
4.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Bard levels 8, 12, and 16.
4.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Bard levels 8, 12, 16, and 19.

5.name: Font of Inspiration
5.text: You now regain all your expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a Short or Long Rest. In addition, you can expend a spell slot (no action required) to regain one expended use of Bardic Inspiration.
5.description: You now regain all your expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

6.name: Subclass Feature
6.text: You gain a feature from your Bard subclass.
6.description: You gain a feature from your Bard subclass.

7.name: Countercharm
7.text: You can use musical notes or words of power to disrupt mind-influencing effects. If you or a creature within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw against an effect that applies the Charmed or Frightened condition, you can take a Reaction to cause the save to be rerolled, and the new roll has Advantage.

actions.name: Countercharm
actions.effect: Reroll a failed save vs Charmed/Frightened with Advantage

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
8.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.
8.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

9.name: Expertise
9.text: You gain Expertise in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.
9.description: You gain Expertise in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

10.name: Magical Secrets
10.text: You've learned secrets from various magical traditions. Whenever you reach a Bard level (including this level) and the Prepared Spells number in the Bard Features table increases, you can choose any of your new prepared spells from the Bard, Cleric, Druid, and Wizard spell lists, and the chosen spells count as Bard spells for you. In addition, whenever you replace a spell prepared for this class, you can replace it with a spell from those lists.

choices.label: Prepared spells may now be drawn from Bard/Cleric/Druid/Wizard lists

10.description: You have plundered magical knowledge from a wide spectrum of disciplines. Choose two spells from any classes, including this one. A chosen spell must be a cantrip or a spell for which you have spell slots. You always have the chosen spells prepared, and they count as Bard spells for you. At higher levels (14 and 18), you add two more spells from any class to your repertoire in the same way.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
12.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.
12.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

14.name: Subclass Feature
14.text: You gain a feature from your Bard subclass.
14.description: You gain a feature from your Bard subclass.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
16.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.
16.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

18.name: Superior Inspiration
18.text: When you roll Initiative, you regain expended uses of Bardic Inspiration until you have two if you have fewer than that.
18.description: When you roll Initiative and have no Bardic Inspiration uses remaining, you regain two uses of it.

19.name: Epic Boon
19.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Spell Recall is recommended.
19.description: You gain the Epic Boon of Luck feat or another Epic Boon feat of your choice.

20.name: Words of Creation
20.text: You have mastered two of the Words of Creation: the words of life and death. You therefore always have the Power Word Heal and Power Word Kill spells prepared. When you cast either spell, you can target a second creature with it if that creature is within 10 feet of the first target.
20.description: You have mastered two of the prime Words of Creation: the words for the Prismatic Wall and Power Word Heal spells. You always have these spells prepared, they count as Bard spells for you, and casting them costs you no spell slots. Once you cast either spell with this feature, you can't cast that spell with it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: College of Dance
subclasses.tagline: Move in Harmony with the Cosmos
subclasses.description: Bards of the College of Dance practice a way of being in harmony with the whirling cosmos that emphasizes agility, speed, and grace.

3.name: Dazzling Footwork
3.text: While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield, you gain: Dance Virtuoso - Advantage on any Charisma (Performance) check that involves you dancing. Unarmored Defense - your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Charisma modifiers. Agile Strikes - when you expend a use of your Bardic Inspiration as part of an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction, you can make one Unarmed Strike as part of that action. Bardic Damage - you can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack rolls of your Unarmed Strikes, and when you deal damage with an Unarmed Strike you can deal Bludgeoning damage equal to a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die plus your Dexterity modifier (this roll doesn't expend the die).

choices.label: AC formula while unarmored & no shield

6.name: Inspiring Movement
6.text: When an enemy you can see ends its turn within 5 feet of you, you can take a Reaction and expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to move up to half your Speed. Then one ally of your choice within 30 feet of you can also move up to half their Speed using their Reaction. None of this movement provokes Opportunity Attacks.

6.name: Tandem Footwork
6.text: When you roll Initiative, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration if you don't have the Incapacitated condition. Roll your Bardic Inspiration die; you and each ally within 30 feet of you who can see or hear you gains a bonus to Initiative equal to the number rolled.

14.name: Leading Evasion
14.text: When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. If any creatures within 5 feet of you are making the same Dexterity saving throw, you can share this benefit with them for that save. You can't use this feature if you have the Incapacitated condition.

features.name: Dazzling Footwork
features.description: Your practice of dance becomes an expressive and magical art. While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield, you gain the following benefits: your base Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Charisma modifier; Dexterity (Acrobatics) is a Bard skill for you, and if it's already a Bard skill, you gain Expertise in it.

features.name: Inspiring Movement
features.description: When an enemy ends its turn within 5 feet of an ally of yours, and that ally isn't Incapacitated, you can use your Reaction and expend one use of Bardic Inspiration to move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. When you stop moving, the ally can also move up to half their Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Neither of you can be moved beyond your Speed by this feature.

features.name: Tandem Footwork
features.description: When you roll Initiative, you can spend one use of Bardic Inspiration if you don't have the Incapacitated condition. When you do so, roll the Bardic Inspiration die and choose a number of creatures you can see within 60 feet of yourself, up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). Each of them gains a bonus to their Initiative equal to the number rolled.

features.name: Leading Evasion
features.description: When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail. If any creatures within 5 feet of you are making the same Dexterity saving throw, you can share this benefit with them for that saving throw.

subclasses.name: College of Glamour
subclasses.tagline: Weave Beguiling Fey Magic
subclasses.description: The College of Glamour traces its origins to the beguiling magic of the Feywild. Bards who study this magic weave threads of beauty and terror into their songs and stories.

3.name: Beguiling Magic
3.text: You always have the Charm Person and Mirror Image spells prepared. Immediately after you cast an Enchantment or Illusion spell using a spell slot, you can cause a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target has the Charmed or Frightened condition (your choice) for 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest, or by expending one use of your Bardic Inspiration (no action required).

3.name: Mantle of Inspiration
3.text: As a Bonus Action, you can expend a use of Bardic Inspiration, rolling a Bardic Inspiration die. Choose a number of other creatures within 60 feet of yourself, up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). Each gains Temporary Hit Points equal to two times the number rolled, and then each can use its Reaction to move up to its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

actions.name: Mantle of Inspiration
actions.effect: Allies gain 2x Bardic die Temp HP and may Reaction-move

6.name: Mantle of Majesty
6.text: You always have the Command spell prepared. As a Bonus Action, you cast Command without expending a spell slot, and you take on an unearthly appearance for 1 minute. During this time, you can cast Command as a Bonus Action without expending a spell slot. Any creature Charmed by you automatically fails its saving throw against the Command you cast with this feature. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest, or by expending a level 3+ spell slot (no action required).

actions.name: Mantle of Majesty
actions.effect: Cast Command free for 1 min; Charmed creatures auto-fail

14.name: Unbreakable Majesty
14.text: As a Bonus Action, you can assume a magically majestic presence for 1 minute or until you have the Incapacitated condition. For the duration, whenever any creature hits you with an attack roll for the first time on a turn, the attacker must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC, or the attack misses instead. Once you assume this majestic presence, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

actions.name: Unbreakable Majesty
actions.effect: For 1 min, attackers must pass a CHA save or their attack misses

features.name: Mantle of Inspiration
features.description: As a bonus action, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration to grant yourself a wondrous appearance. When you do, choose a number of creatures you can see within 60 feet, up to your Charisma modifier. Each of them must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be charmed by you until the end of your next turn. While charmed, it can use its reaction to move up to its speed toward you. It also gains temporary hit points equal to your Bardic Inspiration die + your Charisma modifier.

features.name: Enthralling Performance
features.description: If you perform for at least 1 minute, you can attempt to inspire wonder in your audience. At the end of the performance, choose a number of humanoids within 60 feet up to your Charisma modifier. Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be charmed by you. While charmed, the target idolizes you, speaks glowingly of you, and hinders anyone who opposes you. This effect ends after 1 hour, when the target is harmed, or you are revealed to be a fiend or undead.

features.name: Mantle of Majesty
features.description: As a bonus action, you cast Command without expending a spell slot, and you take on an appearance of unearthly beauty for 1 minute or until your concentration ends. During this time, you can cast Command as a bonus action on each of your turns without expending a spell slot. Any creature charmed by you automatically fails its saving throw against the Command. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Unbreakable Majesty
features.description: As a bonus action, you can assume a magically majestic presence for 1 minute or until you are incapacitated. For the duration, whenever any creature tries to attack you for the first time on a turn, the attacker must make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it can't attack you on this turn and must choose a new target. On a successful save, it can attack you this turn but has disadvantage on the roll. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

subclasses.name: College of Lore
subclasses.tagline: Plumb the Depths of Magical Knowledge
subclasses.description: Bards of the College of Lore collect spells and secrets from diverse sources. The college's members gather in libraries and universities to share their lore.

3.name: Bonus Proficiencies
3.text: You gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.

3.name: Cutting Words
3.text: When a creature that you can see within 60 feet of yourself makes a damage roll or succeeds on an ability check or attack roll, you can take a Reaction to expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration; roll your Bardic Inspiration die, and subtract the number rolled from the creature's roll, reducing the damage or potentially turning the success into a failure.

actions.name: Cutting Words
actions.effect: Subtract a Bardic Inspiration die from an enemy's damage/check/attack roll

6.name: Magical Discoveries
6.text: You learn two spells of your choice. These spells can come from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list or any combination thereof. A spell you choose must be a cantrip or a spell for which you have spell slots. You always have the chosen spells prepared, and whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one of the spells with another spell that meets these requirements.

14.name: Peerless Skill
14.text: When you make an ability check or attack roll and fail, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration; roll the Bardic Inspiration die, and add the number rolled to the d20, potentially turning a failure into a success. On a failure, the Bardic Inspiration isn't expended.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.

features.name: Cutting Words
features.description: When a creature you can see within 60 feet makes an attack roll, ability check, or damage roll, you can use your reaction to expend one Bardic Inspiration die, rolling it and subtracting the number rolled from the creature's roll. You can choose to use this feature after the roll but before the outcome is determined.

features.name: Magical Discoveries
features.description: You learn two spells of your choice from any class. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast or a cantrip. The chosen spells count as Bard spells for you but don't count against the number of Bard spells you know.

features.name: Peerless Skill
features.description: When you make an ability check, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration. Roll the die and add the number to your check. You can choose to do so after you roll the die for the ability check but before the DM says whether it succeeds or fails.

subclasses.name: College of Valor
subclasses.tagline: Sing the Deeds of Ancient Heroes
subclasses.description: Bards of the College of Valor are daring storytellers whose tales preserve the memory of the great heroes of the past. With their songs, they inspire new generations to reach the same heights of accomplishment as the heroes of old.

3.name: Combat Inspiration
3.text: A creature that has a Bardic Inspiration die from you can use it for one of the following effects. Defense: when the creature is hit by an attack roll, it can use its Reaction to roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to its AC against that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss. Offense: immediately after the creature hits a target with an attack roll, it can roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to the attack's damage.

3.name: Martial Training
3.text: You gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Medium armor and Shields. In addition, you can use a Simple or Martial weapon as a Spellcasting Focus to cast spells from your Bard spell list.

6.name: Extra Attack
6.text: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. In addition, you can cast one of your cantrips that has a casting time of an action in place of one of those attacks.

14.name: Battle Magic
14.text: After you cast a spell that has a casting time of an action, you can make one attack with a weapon as a Bonus Action.

features.name: Combat Inspiration
features.description: A creature that has a Bardic Inspiration die from you can roll that die and add the number rolled to a weapon damage roll it just made. Alternatively, when an attack roll is made against the creature, it can use its reaction to roll the die and add the number to its AC against that attack.

features.name: Martial Training
features.description: You gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.description: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Battle Magic
features.description: When you use your action to cast a Bard spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

subclasses.name: College of Spirits
subclasses.tagline: Conjure Spiritual Embodiments of Powerful Forces
subclasses.description: Bards of the College of Spirits seek tales with inherent power - be they legends, histories, or fictions - and bring their subjects to life. Using occult trappings, these bards conjure spiritual embodiments of powerful forces to change the world once more. Such spirits are capricious, though, and what a bard summons isn't always entirely under their control.
subclasses.edition_note: Originally published for 2014 rules; feature levels are as printed in Van Richten's Guide to Ravenloft.

3.name: Guiding Whispers
3.text: You can reach out to spirits to guide you and others. You learn the Guidance cantrip, which doesn't count against the number of bard cantrips you know. For you, it has a range of 60 feet when you cast it.

3.name: Spiritual Focus
3.text: You employ tools that aid you in channeling spirits, be they historical figures or fictional archetypes. You can use the following objects as a spellcasting focus for your bard spells: a candle, crystal ball, skull, spirit board, or tarokka deck. Starting at 6th level, when you cast a bard spell that deals damage or restores hit points through the Spiritual Focus, roll a d6, and you gain a bonus to one damage or healing roll of the spell equal to the number rolled.

3.name: Tales from Beyond
3.text: You reach out to spirits who tell their tales through you. While you are holding your Spiritual Focus, you can use a bonus action to expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration and roll on the Spirit Tales table using your Bardic Inspiration die to determine the tale the spirits direct you to tell. You retain the tale in mind until you bestow the tale's effect or you finish a short or long rest. You can use an action to choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you (this can be you) to be the target of the tale's effect; once you do so, you can't bestow the tale's effect again until you roll it again. You can retain only one tale in mind at a time, and rolling on the Spirit Tales table immediately ends the effect of the previous tale. If the tale requires a saving throw, the DC equals your spell save DC.

choices.label: Spirit Tale (rolled on the Spirit Tales table with your Bardic Inspiration die)

options.name: Tale of the Clever Animal
options.effect: For the next 10 minutes, whenever the target makes an Intelligence, a Wisdom, or a Charisma check, the target can roll an extra die immediately after rolling the d20 and add the extra die's number to the check. The extra die is the same type as your Bardic Inspiration die.

options.name: Tale of the Renowned Duelist
options.effect: You make a melee spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes force damage equal to two rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die + your Charisma modifier.

options.name: Tale of the Beloved Friends
options.effect: The target and another creature of its choice it can see within 5 feet of it gains temporary hit points equal to a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die + your Charisma modifier.

options.name: Tale of the Runaway
options.effect: The target can immediately use its reaction to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. When the target teleports, it can choose a number of creatures it can see within 30 feet of it up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 0) to immediately use the same reaction.

options.name: Tale of the Avenger
options.effect: For 1 minute, any creature that hits the target with a melee attack takes force damage equal to a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die.

options.name: Tale of the Traveler
options.effect: The target gains temporary hit points equal to a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die + your bard level. While it has these temporary hit points, the target's walking speed increases by 10 feet and it gains a +1 bonus to its AC.

options.name: Tale of the Beguiler
options.effect: The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or take psychic damage equal to two rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die, and the target is incapacitated until the end of its next turn.

options.name: Tale of the Phantom
options.effect: The target becomes invisible until the end of its next turn or until it hits a creature with an attack. If the target hits a creature with an attack during this invisibility, the creature it hits takes necrotic damage equal to a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die and is frightened of the target until the end of the frightened creature's next turn.

options.name: Tale of the Brute
options.effect: Each creature of the target's choice it can see within 30 feet of it must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes thunder damage equal to three rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die and is knocked prone. A creature that succeeds takes half as much damage and isn't knocked prone.

options.name: Tale of the Dragon
options.effect: The target spews fire from the mouth in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking fire damage equal to four rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

options.name: Tale of the Angel
options.effect: The target regains hit points equal to two rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die + your Charisma modifier, and you end one condition from the following list affecting the target: blinded, deafened, paralyzed, petrified, or poisoned.

options.name: Tale of the Mind-Bender
options.effect: You evoke an incomprehensible fable from an otherworldly being. The target must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw or take psychic damage equal to three rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die and be stunned until the end of its next turn.

actions.name: Tales from Beyond
actions.effect: Expend one Bardic Inspiration use and roll on the Spirit Tales table

6.name: Spirit Session
6.text: Spirits provide you with supernatural insights. You can conduct an hour-long ritual channeling spirits (which can be done during a short or long rest) using your Spiritual Focus. You can conduct the ritual with a number of willing creatures equal to your proficiency bonus (including yourself). At the end of the ritual, you temporarily learn one spell of your choice from any class. The spell must be of a level equal to the number of creatures that conducted the ritual or less, must be of a level you can cast, and must be in the school of divination or necromancy. The chosen spell counts as a bard spell for you but doesn't count against the number of bard spells you know. Once you perform the ritual, you can't do so again until you start a long rest, and you know the chosen spell until you start a long rest.

14.name: Mystical Connection
14.text: You now have the ability to nudge the spirits of Tales from Beyond toward certain tales. Whenever you roll on the Spirit Tales table, you can roll the die twice and choose which of the two effects to bestow. If you roll the same number on both dice, you can ignore the number and choose any effect on the table.

features.name: Guiding Whispers
features.description: You can reach out to spirits to guide you and others. You learn the Guidance cantrip, which doesn't count against the number of Bard cantrips you know. For you, it has a range of 60 feet when you cast it.

features.name: Spiritual Focus
features.description: You employ tools that channel spiritual energy: a candle, crystal ball, skull, spirit board, or tarokka deck as a spellcasting focus for your Bard spells. Starting at 6th level, when you cast a Bard spell that deals damage or restores hit points using the Spiritual Focus, roll a d6 and you gain a bonus to one damage or healing roll equal to the number rolled.

features.name: Tales from Beyond
features.description: You reach out to spirits who tell their tales through you. While holding your Spiritual Focus, you can use a bonus action to expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration and roll on the Spirit Tales table using your Bardic Inspiration die. You retain the tale in mind until you bestow it or finish a Short or Long Rest. You can use an action to bestow the tale on a creature within 30 feet. The tale manifests as a brief magical effect unique to each entry on the Spirit Tales table.

features.name: Spiritual Focus Bonus
features.description: When you cast a Bard spell that deals damage or restores hit points through your Spiritual Focus, roll a d6 and add the number to one damage or healing roll of the spell.

features.name: Mystical Connection
features.description: You now have the ability to channel spirits more effectively. Whenever you use your Tales from Beyond feature, you can roll the die twice and choose which of the two effects to bestow. If you roll the same number on both dice, you can ignore the number and choose any effect on the Spirit Tales table.

subclasses.name: College of Swords
subclasses.edition_note: Originally published for 2014 rules in Xanathar's Guide to Everything; feature levels are as printed in that book.
subclasses.tagline: Entertain Through Daring Feats of Weapon Prowess
subclasses.description: Bards of the College of Swords are called blades, and they entertain through daring feats of weapon prowess. Though they use their weapons to entertain, they are also highly trained and skilled warriors in their own right.

3.name: Bonus Proficiencies
3.text: When you join the College of Swords at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with medium armor and the scimitar. If you're proficient with a simple or martial melee weapon, you can use it as a spellcasting focus for your bard spells.

3.name: Fighting Style
3.text: You adopt a style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if something in the game lets you choose again. Dueling: When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon. Two-Weapon Fighting: When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.

3.name: Blade Flourish
3.text: You learn to perform impressive displays of martial prowess and speed. Whenever you take the Attack action on your turn, your walking speed increases by 10 feet until the end of the turn, and if a weapon attack that you make as part of this action hits a creature, you can use one of the following Blade Flourish options of your choice. You can use only one Blade Flourish option per turn. Defensive Flourish: Expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to cause the weapon to deal extra damage equal to the number you roll on the Bardic Inspiration die; you also add the number rolled to your AC until the start of your next turn. Slashing Flourish: Expend one use of Bardic Inspiration to cause the weapon to deal extra damage equal to the number you roll on the die to the target you hit and to any other creature of your choice within 5 feet of you. Mobile Flourish: Expend one use of Bardic Inspiration to cause extra damage equal to the number you roll on the die; you can also push the target up to 5 feet away from you, plus a number of feet equal to the number you roll, and then immediately use your reaction to move up to your walking speed to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target.

6.name: Extra Attack
6.text: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

14.name: Master's Flourish
14.text: Whenever you use a Blade Flourish option, you can roll a d6 and use it instead of expending a Bardic Inspiration die.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency with medium armor and scimitars. If you're proficient with a simple or martial melee weapon, you can use it as a spellcasting focus for your Bard spells.

features.name: Blade Flourish
features.description: Whenever you take the Attack action on your turn, your walking speed increases by 10 feet until the end of the turn, and if a weapon attack that you make as part of this action hits a creature, you can use one of the following Blade Flourish options of your choice: Defensive Flourish (spend one Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to your AC until the start of your next turn and to the damage of the triggering attack), Slashing Flourish (spend one die and deal the extra damage to the target and all creatures within 5 feet), Mobile Flourish (spend one die and push the target 5 + the die roll feet away, then move up to your speed toward it as a reaction).

features.name: Extra Attack
features.description: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Master's Flourish
features.description: Whenever you use a Blade Flourish option, you can roll a d6 and use it instead of expending a Bardic Inspiration die.

subclasses.name: College of Whispers
subclasses.edition_note: Originally published for 2014 rules in Xanathar's Guide to Everything; feature levels are as printed in that book.
subclasses.tagline: Wolves Among Sheep Who Trade in Secrets
subclasses.description: Bards of the College of Whispers appear to be like other bards, but in truth this college teaches its students that they are wolves among sheep. These bards use their knowledge and magic to uncover secrets and turn them against others through extortion and threats.

3.name: Psychic Blades
3.text: You gain the ability to make your weapon attacks magically toxic to a creature's mind. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to deal an extra 2d6 psychic damage to that target. You can do so only once per round on your turn. The psychic damage increases when you reach certain levels in this class, increasing to 3d6 at 5th level, 5d6 at 10th level, and 8d6 at 15th level.

3.name: Words of Terror
3.text: You learn to infuse innocent-seeming words with an insidious magic that can inspire terror. If you speak to a humanoid alone for at least 1 minute, you can attempt to seed paranoia in its mind. At the end of the conversation, the target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be frightened of you or another creature of your choice. The target is frightened in this way for 1 hour, until it is attacked or damaged, or until it witnesses its allies being attacked or damaged. If the target succeeds on its saving throw, the target has no hint that you tried to frighten it. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

6.name: Mantle of Whispers
6.text: You gain the ability to adopt a humanoid's persona. When a humanoid dies within 30 feet of you, you can magically capture its shadow using your reaction. You retain this shadow until you use it or you finish a long rest. You can use the shadow as an action: it vanishes, magically transforming into a disguise that appears on you, making you look like the dead person but healthy and alive. This disguise lasts for 1 hour or until you end it as a bonus action. While disguised, you gain access to all information the humanoid would freely share with a casual acquaintance (general background and personal life, but not secrets), enough to pass yourself off as the person by drawing on its memories. Another creature can see through this disguise by succeeding on a Wisdom (Insight) check contested by your Charisma (Deception) check; you gain a +5 bonus to your check. Once you capture a shadow with this feature, you can't capture another until you finish a short or long rest.

14.name: Shadow Lore
14.text: You gain the ability to weave dark magic into your words and tap into a creature's deepest fears. As an action, you magically whisper a phrase that only one creature of your choice within 30 feet of you can hear. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC; it automatically succeeds if it doesn't share a language with you or if it can't hear you. On a successful save, your whisper sounds like unintelligible mumbling and has no effect. On a failed save, the target is charmed by you for the next 8 hours or until you or your allies attack it, damage it, or force it to make a saving throw; it interprets the whispers as a description of its most mortifying secret. You gain no knowledge of this secret, but the target is convinced you know it. The charmed creature obeys your commands for fear that you will reveal its secret (it won't risk its life or fight for you unless already inclined to), and grants you favors and gifts it would offer a close friend. When the effect ends, the creature has no understanding of why it held you in such fear. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

features.name: Psychic Blades
features.description: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration to deal an extra 2d6 psychic damage to the target. You can do this only once per round on your turn. The psychic damage increases when you reach certain levels: 3d6 at 5th level, 5d6 at 10th level, and 8d6 at 15th level.

features.name: Words of Terror
features.description: You can speak a message to a humanoid that can hear you for at least 1 minute. At the end, the target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target is frightened of you or another creature of your choice for 1 hour. On a success, the target doesn't realize you tried to frighten it. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Mantle of Whispers
features.description: When a humanoid dies within 30 feet of you, you can magically capture its shadow as a reaction. The shadow retains the creature's appearance, racial features, class features, and proficiencies for 1 hour or until you capture another shadow. While wearing the shadow, you appear as the dead creature. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Shadow Lore
features.description: As an action, you magically whisper a phrase that only one creature of your choice within 30 feet can hear. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target is charmed by you for 8 hours or until it takes damage. While charmed, the target obeys your commands. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Mote of Potential
features.description: Whenever you give a creature a Bardic Inspiration die, you can utter a note from the Song of Creation to create a Mote of Potential, which orbits within 5 feet of that creature. The mote is intangible and invulnerable, and it lasts until the Bardic Inspiration die is lost. A creature can have only one mote at a time. When the creature uses the Bardic Inspiration die, the mote provides an additional effect based on the use: attack roll (the creature or one creature hit by the attack takes Thunder damage equal to the Bardic Inspiration die), ability check (the creature or one creature within 30 ft can use a Reaction to take the Bardic Inspiration die result and add it as a bonus to their ability check), or saving throw (one creature within 30 ft has advantage on the next saving throw or attack roll they make before the end of their next turn).

features.name: Performance of Creation
