features.description: As an action, you can channel the magic of the Song of Creation to create one nonmagical item of your choice in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of you. The item must appear on a surface or in a liquid that can support it. The total of your Bard level and the item's gp value must be 20 or less, and the item can't be a magic item. The item disappears after a number of hours equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest, unless you expend a spell slot of 2nd level or higher to use it again. You can have only one item created by this feature at a time.

features.name: Animating Performance
features.description: As an action, you can animate one Large or smaller nonmagical item within 30 feet of you that isn't being worn or carried. The animate item uses the Dancing Item stat block, which uses your spell save DC and Proficiency Bonus. The item is an ally to you and your companions. In combat, the item shares your Initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your verbal commands (no action required by you). If you don't issue any, it takes the Dodge action and uses its move to avoid danger. The animation lasts for 1 hour, until the item is reduced to 0 HP, or until you die. Once you animate an item with this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest, unless you expend a spell slot of 3rd level or higher to use this feature again.

features.name: Creative Crescendo
features.description: When you use your Performance of Creation feature, you can create more than one item at once. The number of items equals your Charisma modifier (minimum of two items). If you create an item that would exceed your limit, you choose which of the previously created items disappears. Only one of these items can be of the maximum size and value you can create; the rest must be Small or Tiny.

features.name: Silver Tongue
features.description: You are a master at saying the right thing at the right time. When you make a Charisma (Persuasion) or Charisma (Deception) check, you can treat a roll of 9 or lower on the d20 as a 10.

features.name: Unsettling Words
features.description: You can spin words laced with magic that unsettle a creature and cause it to doubt itself. As a Bonus Action, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration and choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. Roll the Bardic Inspiration die. The creature must subtract the number rolled from the next saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn.

features.name: Unfailing Inspiration
features.description: Your inspiring words are so persuasive that others feel driven to succeed. When a creature uses one of your Bardic Inspiration dice and the check fails, that creature can keep the Bardic Inspiration die.

features.name: Universal Speech
features.description: You have gained the ability to make your speech intelligible to any creature. As an action, choose one or more creatures within 60 feet of you, up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). The chosen creatures can magically understand you, regardless of the language you speak, for 1 hour. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest, unless you expend a spell slot of any level to use it again.

features.name: Infectious Inspiration
features.description: When you successfully inspire someone, the power of your eloquence can now spread to someone else. When a creature uses one of your Bardic Inspiration dice and the check succeeds, you can use your Reaction to give a different creature (other than yourself) within 60 feet of you a Bardic Inspiration die without expending any of your Bardic Inspiration uses. You can use this Reaction a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

options.name: Option A
options.text: Chain Shirt, Shield, Mace, Holy Symbol, Priest's Pack, and 7 GP

options.name: Option B
options.text: 110 GP

1.name: Spellcasting
1.text: You have learned to cast spells through prayer and meditation. Cantrips: you know three cantrips of your choice from the Cleric spell list (Guidance, Sacred Flame, and Thaumaturgy recommended); you learn another at Cleric levels 4 and 10. Spell Slots: the Cleric Features table shows how many spell slots you have; you regain all expended slots on a Long Rest. Prepared Spells of Level 1+: you prepare a list of level 1+ Cleric spells, starting with four level 1 spells; the number increases as you gain levels, and you can change the list whenever you finish a Long Rest. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability. You can use a Holy Symbol as a Spellcasting Focus.

choices.label: Prepared Spells (from Cleric list; count per progression_table)

1.description: You have learned to cast divine spells through prayer and meditation. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability. You can prepare a number of spells equal to your Wisdom modifier plus your Cleric level.

1.name: Divine Order
1.text: You have dedicated yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice.

options.name: Protector
options.text: Trained for battle, you gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Heavy armor.

options.name: Thaumaturge
options.text: You know one extra cantrip from the Cleric spell list. In addition, your mystical connection to the divine gives you a bonus to your Intelligence (Arcana or Religion) checks equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1).

1.description: You have dedicated yourself to one of two divine roles: Protector (you gain proficiency with Martial weapons and Heavy armor) or Thaumaturge (you know one additional cantrip from the Cleric spell list and your choice of the Arcana or Religion skill).

2.name: Channel Divinity
2.text: You can channel divine energy directly from the Outer Planes to fuel magical effects. You start with two effects: Divine Spark and Turn Undead. You can use Channel Divinity twice; you regain one expended use on a Short Rest and all on a Long Rest (additional uses at higher levels per the table). If a Channel Divinity effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals your Cleric spell save DC. Divine Spark: as a Magic action, point your Holy Symbol at a creature within 30 feet; roll 1d8 and add your Wisdom modifier, then either restore that many Hit Points or force a Constitution save for that much Necrotic or Radiant damage (half on success). You roll an additional d8 at Cleric levels 7 (2d8), 13 (3d8), and 18 (4d8). Turn Undead: as a Magic action, present your Holy Symbol; each Undead of your choice within 30 feet must make a Wisdom save or have the Frightened and Incapacitated conditions for 1 minute, trying to move away from you (ends early if it takes damage).

actions.name: Channel Divinity: Divine Spark
actions.effect: 1d8 + WIS healing OR Necrotic/Radiant damage (CON save, half on success); scales 2d8@7, 3d8@13, 4d8@18

actions.name: Channel Divinity: Turn Undead
actions.effect: Undead within 30 ft make WIS save or Frightened + Incapacitated 1 min

2.description: You can channel divine energy directly from the Multiverse to fuel magical effects. You start with two such effects: Divine Spark and Turn Undead. Each time you use Channel Divinity, you choose which effect to create, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest. Starting at level 6 you can use it twice per rest, and at level 18 three times.

3.name: Cleric Subclass
3.text: You gain a Cleric subclass of your choice. The Life Domain, Light Domain, Trickery Domain, and War Domain subclasses are detailed in this class's subclasses array.
3.description: You gain a Cleric subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Cleric levels, and lets you channel divinity for new effects.

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
4.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Cleric levels 8, 12, and 16.
4.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Cleric levels 8, 12, 16, and 19.

5.name: Sear Undead
5.text: Whenever you use Turn Undead, you can roll a number of d8s equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1d8) and add the rolls together. Each Undead that fails its saving throw against that use of Turn Undead takes Radiant damage equal to the roll's total. This damage doesn't end the turn effect.
5.description: Whenever you use Turn Undead, you can roll a number of d8s equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1d8) and add the rolls together. Each Undead that fails its saving throw against that use of Turn Undead takes Radiant damage equal to the roll's total. This damage doesn't end the condition imposed by Turn Undead.

6.name: Subclass Feature
6.text: You gain a feature from your Cleric subclass.
6.description: You gain a feature from your Cleric subclass.

7.name: Blessed Strikes
7.text: Divine power infuses you in battle. You gain one of the following options of your choice.

options.name: Divine Strike
options.text: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon, you can cause the target to take an extra 1d8 Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice).

options.name: Potent Spellcasting
options.text: Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Cleric cantrip.

7.description: Divine power infuses you in battle. When you hit a creature with an attack using a weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can also deal 1d8 Radiant or Necrotic damage (your choice) to the target. Once you deal this damage, you can't use this feature again until the start of your next turn.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
8.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.
8.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

10.name: Divine Intervention
10.text: You can call on your deity or pantheon to intervene on your behalf. As a Magic action, choose any Cleric spell of level 5 or lower that doesn't require a Reaction to cast. As part of the same action, you cast that spell without expending a spell slot or needing Material components. You can't use this feature again until you finish a Long Rest.

actions.name: Divine Intervention
actions.effect: Cast any Cleric spell of level 5 or lower for free

10.description: You can call on your deity or pantheon to intervene on your behalf. As a Magic action, choose any Cleric spell of level 5 or lower that doesn't require a Reaction to cast. As part of the same action, you cast that spell without expending a spell slot or needing Material components. You can't use this feature again until you finish a Long Rest.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
12.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.
12.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

14.name: Improved Blessed Strikes
14.text: The option you chose for Blessed Strikes grows more powerful. Divine Strike: the extra damage of your Divine Strike increases to 2d8. Potent Spellcasting: when you cast a Cleric cantrip and deal damage to a creature with it, you can give vitality to yourself or another creature within 60 feet of yourself, granting a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Wisdom modifier.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
16.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.
16.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

17.name: Subclass Feature
17.text: You gain a feature from your Cleric subclass.
17.description: You gain a feature from your Cleric subclass.

19.name: Epic Boon
19.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Fate is recommended.
19.description: You gain the Epic Boon of Fate feat or another Epic Boon feat of your choice.

20.name: Greater Divine Intervention
20.text: You can call on even more powerful divine intervention. When you use your Divine Intervention feature, you can choose Wish when you select a spell. If you do so, you can't use Divine Intervention again until you finish 2d4 Long Rests.
20.description: Your Divine Intervention now allows you to cast any Cleric spell, including one of level 6–9, without a slot or material components.

subclasses.name: Life Domain
subclasses.tagline: Soothe the Hurts of the World
subclasses.description: The Life Domain focuses on the positive energy that helps sustain all life in the multiverse. Clerics who tap into this domain are masters of healing.

3.name: Life Domain Spells
3.text: Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells prepared when you reach the listed Cleric levels.

3.name: Disciple of Life
3.text: When a spell you cast with a spell slot restores Hit Points to a creature, that creature regains additional Hit Points on the turn you cast the spell. The additional Hit Points equal 2 plus the spell slot's level.

3.name: Preserve Life
3.text: As a Magic action, you present your Holy Symbol and expend a use of your Channel Divinity to evoke healing energy that can restore a number of Hit Points equal to five times your Cleric level. Choose Bloodied creatures within 30 feet of yourself (which can include you), and divide those Hit Points among them. This feature can restore a creature to no more than half its Hit Point maximum.

actions.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
actions.effect: Restore HP equal to 5x Cleric level, divided among Bloodied creatures (max half HP each)

6.name: Blessed Healer
6.text: The healing spells you cast on others heal you as well. Immediately after you cast a spell with a spell slot that restores Hit Points to one or more creatures other than yourself, you regain Hit Points equal to 2 plus the spell slot's level.

17.name: Supreme Healing
17.text: When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore Hit Points to a creature with a spell or Channel Divinity, don't roll those dice for the healing; instead use the highest number possible for each die.

features.name: Bonus Proficiency
features.description: You gain proficiency with heavy armor.

features.name: Disciple of Life
features.description: Your healing spells are more effective. Whenever you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore hit points to a creature, the creature regains additional hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

features.name: Life Domain Spells
features.description: Your divine connection to life grants you the following spells: 1st (Bless, Cure Wounds), 3rd (Lesser Restoration, Prayer of Healing), 5th (Mass Healing Word, Revivify), 7th (Aura of Life, Death Ward), 9th (Greater Restoration, Mass Cure Wounds). These spells are always prepared and don't count against your Cleric spell count.

features.name: Blessed Healer
features.description: The healing spells you cast on others heal you as well. When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that restores hit points to a creature other than you, you regain hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

features.name: Supreme Healing
features.description: When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell, you instead use the highest number possible for each die. For example, instead of restoring 2d6 hit points to a creature, you restore 12.

subclasses.name: Light Domain
subclasses.tagline: Bring Light to Banish Darkness
subclasses.description: The Light Domain emphasizes the divine power to bring about blazing fire and revelation. Clerics who wield this power are enlightened souls infused with radiance.

3.name: Light Domain Spells
3.text: Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells prepared when you reach the listed Cleric levels.

3.name: Radiance of the Dawn
3.text: As a Magic action, you present your Holy Symbol and expend a use of your Channel Divinity to emit a flash of light in a 30-foot Emanation originating from yourself. Any magical Darkness in that area is dispelled. Additionally, each creature of your choice in that area must make a Constitution saving throw, taking Radiant damage equal to 2d10 plus your Cleric level on a failed save or half as much on a success.

actions.name: Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn
actions.effect: Dispel magical Darkness; CON save or 2d10 + Cleric level Radiant damage

3.name: Warding Flare
3.text: When a creature that you can see within 30 feet of yourself makes an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to impose Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), regaining all uses on a Long Rest.

actions.name: Warding Flare
actions.effect: Impose Disadvantage on an attack roll

6.name: Improved Warding Flare
6.text: You regain all expended uses of your Warding Flare when you finish a Short or Long Rest. In addition, whenever you use Warding Flare, you can give the target of the triggering attack a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to 2d6 plus your Wisdom modifier.

17.name: Corona of Light
17.text: As a Magic action, you cause yourself to emit an aura of sunlight that lasts for 1 minute or until you dismiss it. You emit Bright Light in a 60-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 30 feet. Your enemies in the Bright Light have Disadvantage on saving throws against your Radiance of the Dawn and any spell that deals Fire or Radiant damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier, regaining all uses on a Long Rest.

actions.name: Corona of Light
actions.effect: Enemies in the light have Disadvantage on saves vs Radiance of the Dawn and Fire/Radiant spells

features.name: Warding Flare
features.description: You can interpose divine light between yourself and an attacking enemy. When you are attacked by a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll, causing light to flare before the attacker before it hits or misses. An attacker that can't be blinded is immune to this feature. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Light Domain Spells
features.description: Your divine connection to light grants you the following spells: 1st (Burning Hands, Faerie Fire), 3rd (Flaming Sphere, Scorching Ray), 5th (Daylight, Fireball), 7th (Guardian of Faith, Wall of Fire), 9th (Flame Strike, Scrying). These are always prepared.

features.name: Bonus Cantrip
features.description: You gain the Light cantrip if you don't already know it. It doesn't count against your number of Cleric cantrips known.

features.name: Radiance of the Dawn
features.description: As an action, you present your holy symbol and dispel any magical darkness within 30 feet of you. Additionally, each hostile creature within 30 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw. A creature takes 2d10 + your Cleric level radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. Creatures with total cover are not affected. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Corona of Light
features.description: As an action, you can activate an aura of sunlight that lasts for 1 minute or until you dismiss it using another action. You emit bright light in a 60-foot radius and dim light 30 feet beyond that. Your enemies in the bright light have disadvantage on saving throws against any spell that deals fire or radiant damage.

subclasses.name: Trickery Domain
subclasses.tagline: Make Mischief and Challenge Authority
subclasses.description: The Trickery Domain offers magic of deception, illusion, and stealth. Clerics who wield this magic are a disruptive force, puncturing pride and mocking tyrants.

3.name: Trickery Domain Spells
3.text: Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells prepared when you reach the listed Cleric levels.

3.name: Blessing of the Trickster
3.text: As a Magic action, you can choose yourself or a willing creature within 30 feet of yourself to have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. This blessing lasts until you finish a Long Rest or you use this feature again.

3.name: Invoke Duplicity
3.text: As a Bonus Action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to create a perfect visual illusion of yourself in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of yourself. The illusion is intangible, lasts 1 minute (ends early if dismissed or Incapacitated), and mimics your expressions and gestures. While it persists: Cast Spells - you can cast spells as though you were in the illusion's space, using your own senses. Distract - when both you and your illusion are within 5 feet of a creature that can see the illusion, you have Advantage on attack rolls against it. Move - as a Bonus Action, you can move the illusion up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see within 120 feet of yourself.

actions.name: Channel Divinity: Invoke Duplicity
actions.effect: Create an illusory duplicate for 1 min; cast spells from its space, gain Advantage when flanking with it

6.name: Trickster's Transposition
6.text: Whenever you take the Bonus Action to create or move the illusion of your Invoke Duplicity, you can teleport, swapping places with the illusion.

17.name: Improved Duplicity
17.text: The illusion of your Invoke Duplicity has grown more powerful. Shared Distraction: when you and your allies make attack rolls against a creature within 5 feet of the illusion, the attack rolls have Advantage. Healing Illusion: when the illusion ends, you or a creature of your choice within 5 feet of it regains a number of Hit Points equal to your Cleric level.

features.name: Blessing of the Trickster
features.description: You can use your action to touch a willing creature (not yourself) to give it advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. This blessing lasts for 1 hour or until you use this feature again.

features.name: Trickery Domain Spells
features.description: Your divine connection to trickery grants you the following spells: 1st (Charm Person, Disguise Self), 3rd (Mirror Image, Pass without Trace), 5th (Blink, Dispel Magic), 7th (Dimension Door, Polymorph), 9th (Dominate Person, Modify Memory). These are always prepared.

features.name: Invoke Duplicity
features.description: As an action, you create a perfect illusory duplicate of yourself that lasts for 1 minute or until you lose your concentration. As a bonus action on your turn, you can move the illusion up to 30 feet to a space you can see. For the duration, you can cast spells as though you were in the illusion's space, but you must use your own senses. Additionally, when both you and your illusion are within 5 feet of a creature, you have advantage on attack rolls against that creature. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Improved Duplicity
features.description: You can create up to four duplicates of yourself, instead of one, when you use Invoke Duplicity. As a bonus action on your turn, you can move any number of them up to 30 feet, to a maximum range of 120 feet.

subclasses.name: War Domain
subclasses.tagline: Inspire Valor and Smite Foes
subclasses.description: War has many manifestations. Clerics of the War Domain excel in battle, inspiring others to fight the good fight and channeling divine power into martial prowess.

3.name: War Domain Spells
3.text: Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells prepared when you reach the listed Cleric levels.

3.name: War Priest
3.text: As a Bonus Action, you can make one attack with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike. You can use this Bonus Action a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), regaining all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

actions.name: War Priest
actions.effect: Make one weapon or Unarmed Strike attack

6.name: War God's Blessing
6.text: You can expend a use of your Channel Divinity to cast Shield of Faith or Spiritual Weapon rather than expending a spell slot. When you cast either spell in this way, the spell doesn't require Concentration; instead it lasts for 1 minute, ending early if you cast that spell again, have the Incapacitated condition, or die.

17.name: Avatar of Battle
17.text: You gain Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

features.name: War Priest
features.description: Your god delivers bolts of inspiration to you while you are engaged in battle. When you use the Attack action, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: War Domain Spells
features.description: Your divine connection to war grants you the following spells: 1st (Divine Favor, Shield of Faith), 3rd (Magic Weapon, Spiritual Weapon), 5th (Crusader's Mantle, Spirit Guardians), 7th (Freedom of Movement, Stoneskin), 9th (Destructive Wave, Hold Monster). These are always prepared.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

features.name: War God's Blessing
features.description: When a creature within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, you can use your reaction to grant that creature a +10 bonus to the roll. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Avatar of Battle
features.description: You gain resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage from nonmagical weapons.

subclasses.name: Forge Domain
subclasses.edition_note: Originally published for 2014 rules in Xanathar's Guide to Everything; feature levels are as printed in that book.
subclasses.tagline: Patron of Artisans Who Work with Metal
subclasses.description: The gods of the forge are patrons of artisans who work with metal, from a humble blacksmith to the mighty elf artisan whose diamond-tipped arrows of mithral have felled demon lords. The gods of the forge teach that, with patience and hard work, even the most intractable metal can be transformed. Deities of this domain include Gond, Reorx, Onatar, Moradin, Hephaestus, and Goibhniu.

1.name: Forge Domain Spells
1.text: You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed. They are always prepared and don't count against the number of spells you can prepare. Cleric level 1: Identify, Searing Smite. Level 3: Heat Metal, Magic Weapon. Level 5: Elemental Weapon, Protection from Energy. Level 7: Fabricate, Wall of Fire. Level 9: Animate Objects, Creation.

1.name: Bonus Proficiencies
1.text: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools.

1.name: Blessing of the Forge
1.text: You gain the ability to imbue magic into a weapon or armor. At the end of a long rest, you can touch one nonmagical object that is a suit of armor or a simple or martial weapon. Until the end of your next long rest or until you die, the object becomes a magic item, granting a +1 bonus to AC if it's armor or a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls if it's a weapon. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

2.name: Channel Divinity: Artisan's Blessing
2.text: You can use your Channel Divinity to create simple items. You conduct an hour-long ritual that crafts a nonmagical item that must include some metal: a simple or martial weapon, a suit of armor, ten pieces of ammunition, a set of tools, or another metal object. The creation is completed at the end of the hour, coalescing in an unoccupied space on a surface within 5 feet of you. The thing you create can be something worth no more than 100 gp. As part of the ritual, you must lay out metal (which can include coins) with a value equal to the creation; the metal irretrievably coalesces and transforms into the creation at the ritual's end. The ritual can create a duplicate of a nonmagical item that contains metal, such as a key, if you possess the original during the ritual.

6.name: Soul of the Forge
6.text: Your mastery of the forge grants you special abilities: you gain resistance to fire damage; and while wearing heavy armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

8.name: Divine Strike
8.text: You gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with the fiery power of the forge. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 fire damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

14.name: Divine Strike (2d8)
14.text: The extra fire damage from your Divine Strike increases to 2d8.

17.name: Saint of Forge and Fire
17.text: Your blessed affinity with fire and metal becomes more powerful: you gain immunity to fire damage; and while wearing heavy armor, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools.

features.name: Forge Domain Spells
features.description: Your divine connection to the forge grants you the following spells: 1st (Identify, Searing Smite), 3rd (Heat Metal, Magic Weapon), 5th (Elemental Weapon, Protection from Energy), 7th (Fabricate, Wall of Fire), 9th (Animate Objects, Creation). These are always prepared.

features.name: Blessing of the Forge
features.description: At the end of a Long Rest, you can touch one nonmagical object that is a suit of armor or a simple or martial weapon. Until the end of your next Long Rest, the object becomes a magic item granting a +1 bonus to AC (if armor) or attack and damage rolls (if weapon). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Soul of the Forge
features.description: Your mastery of the forge grants you special abilities: you gain resistance to fire damage, and while wearing heavy armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

features.name: Saint of Forge and Fire
features.description: Your blessed affinity with fire and metal becomes more powerful. You gain immunity to fire damage. While wearing heavy armor, you have resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

subclasses.name: Grave Domain
subclasses.edition_note: Originally published for 2014 rules in Xanathar's Guide to Everything; feature levels are as printed in that book.
subclasses.tagline: Watch Over the Line Between Life and Death
subclasses.description: Gods of the grave watch over the line between life and death. To these deities, death and the afterlife are a foundational part of the multiverse; to desecrate the peace of the dead is an abomination. Deities of the grave include Kelemvor, Wee Jas, the ancestral spirits of the Undying Court, Hades, Anubis, and Osiris.

1.name: Grave Domain Spells
1.text: You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed. They are always prepared and don't count against the number of spells you can prepare. Cleric level 1: Bane, False Life. Level 3: Gentle Repose, Ray of Enfeeblement. Level 5: Revivify, Vampiric Touch. Level 7: Blight, Death Ward. Level 9: Antilife Shell, Raise Dead.

1.name: Circle of Mortality
1.text: You gain the ability to manipulate the line between life and death. When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell to a creature at 0 hit points, you instead use the highest number possible for each die. In addition, you learn the Spare the Dying cantrip, which doesn't count against the number of cleric cantrips you know; for you, it has a range of 30 feet, and you can cast it as a bonus action.

1.name: Eyes of the Grave
1.text: You gain the ability to occasionally sense the presence of the undead. As an action, you can open your awareness to magically detect undead. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any undead within 60 feet of you that isn't behind total cover and that isn't protected from divination magic. This sense doesn't tell you anything about a creature's capabilities or identity. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

choices.label: Eyes of the Grave uses (= Wisdom modifier, min 1)

2.name: Channel Divinity: Path to the Grave
2.text: You can use your Channel Divinity to mark another creature's life force for termination. As an action, you choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you, cursing it until the end of your next turn. The next time you or an ally of yours hits the cursed creature with an attack, the creature has vulnerability to all of that attack's damage, and then the curse ends.

6.name: Sentinel at Death's Door
6.text: You gain the ability to impede death's progress. As a reaction when you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you suffers a critical hit, you can turn that hit into a normal hit; any effects triggered by a critical hit are canceled. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

choices.label: Sentinel at Death's Door uses (= Wisdom modifier, min 1)

8.name: Potent Spellcasting
8.text: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

17.name: Keeper of Souls
17.text: You can seize a trace of vitality from a parting soul and use it to heal the living. When an enemy you can see dies within 60 feet of you, you or one creature of your choice within 60 feet of you regains hit points equal to the enemy's number of Hit Dice. You can use this feature only if you aren't incapacitated. Once you use it, you can't do so again until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Circle of Mortality
features.description: You gain the ability to manipulate the line between life and death. When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell to a creature at 0 hit points, you instead use the highest number possible for each die. In addition, you learn the Spare the Dying cantrip, which doesn't count against the number of Cleric cantrips you know. For you, it has a range of 30 feet.

features.name: Grave Domain Spells
features.description: Your divine connection to death and resurrection grants you the following spells: 1st (Bane, False Life), 3rd (Gentle Repose, Ray of Enfeeblement), 5th (Revivify, Vampiric Touch), 7th (Blight, Death Ward), 9th (Antilife Shell, Raise Dead). These are always prepared.

features.name: Eyes of the Grave
features.description: As an action, you can open your awareness to magically detect undead. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any undead within 60 feet of you that isn't behind total cover and that isn't protected from divination magic. This sense doesn't tell you anything about a creature's capabilities or identity. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier. You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Sentinel at Death's Door
features.description: As a reaction when you or a creature you can see within 30 feet suffers a critical hit, you can turn that hit into a normal hit. Any effects triggered by a critical hit are canceled. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier. You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Keeper of Souls
features.description: You can seize a trace of vitality from a parting soul and use it to heal the living. When a creature dies within 60 feet of you, you can use your reaction to regain hit points or have a creature within 60 feet regain hit points equal to the creature's number of Hit Dice. You can't use this feature if the creature that died is Undead or a Construct. Once you use it, you can't use it again until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Domain Spells
features.description: You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed: 1st (Command, Heroism), 3rd (Hold Person, Zone of Truth), 5th (Mass Healing Word, Slow), 7th (Compulsion, Locate Creature), 9th (Commune, Dominate Person).

features.name: Voice of Authority
features.description: You can invoke the power of law to drive a teammate to attack. If you cast a spell with a spell slot of 1st level or higher and target an ally with the spell, that ally can use their Reaction immediately after the spell to make one weapon attack against a creature of your choice that you can see.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Order's Demand
features.description: As an action, you exert an awe-inspiring aura. Each creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be Charmed by you until the end of your next turn or until the charmed creature takes any damage. You can also cause any of the Charmed creatures to drop what they are holding when they fail the saving throw.

features.name: Embodiment of the Law
features.description: You have become remarkably adept at channeling magical energy to compel others. If you cast a spell of the Enchantment school using a spell slot of 1st level or higher, you can change the spell's casting time to a Bonus Action for this casting, provided the spell's casting time is normally 1 action. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.description: You gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 Psychic damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

features.name: Order's Wrath
features.description: Enemies you designate for destruction wilt under the combined efforts of you and your allies. If you deal your Divine Strike damage to a creature on your turn, you can curse that creature until the start of your next turn. The next time one of your allies hits the cursed creature with an attack, the target also takes 2d8 Psychic damage, and the curse ends. You can curse a creature in this way only once per turn.

features.name: Domain Spells
features.description: 1st: Heroism, Sanctuary; 3rd: Aid, Warding Bond; 5th: Beacon of Hope, Sending; 7th: Aura of Purity, Otiluke's Resilient Sphere; 9th: Greater Restoration, Rary's Telepathic Bond.

features.name: Implement of Peace
features.description: You gain proficiency in the Insight, Performance, or Persuasion skill (your choice).

features.name: Emboldening Bond
features.description: You can forge an empowering bond among people who are at peace with one another. As an action, you choose a number of willing creatures within 30 feet of you (this can include yourself) equal to your Proficiency Bonus. You create a magical bond among them for 10 minutes or until you use this feature again. While any bonded creature is within 30 feet of another, the creature can roll a d4 and add the number rolled to an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw it makes. Each creature can add the d4 no more than once per turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Balm of Peace
features.description: As an action, you can move up to your speed, without provoking opportunity attacks, and when you move within 5 feet of any other creature during this action, you can restore a number of hit points to that creature equal to 2d6 + your Wisdom modifier (once per creature). A creature can receive this healing only once whenever you take this action.

features.name: Protective Bond
features.description: The bond you forge between people helps them protect each other. When a creature affected by your Emboldening Bond feature is about to take damage, a second bonded creature within 30 feet of the first can use its Reaction to teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the first creature and take all the damage instead.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
features.description: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

features.name: Expansive Bond
features.description: The benefits of your Emboldening Bond and Protective Bond features now work when the bonded creatures are within 60 feet of each other. Moreover, when a creature uses Protective Bond to take another's damage, the creature has Resistance to that damage.

features.name: Domain Spells
features.description: 1st: Faerie Fire, Sleep; 3rd: Moonbeam, See Invisibility; 5th: Aura of Vitality, Leomund's Tiny Hut; 7th: Aura of Life, Greater Invisibility; 9th: Circle of Power, Mislead.

features.name: Eyes of Night
features.description: You can see through the deepest gloom. You have Darkvision out to a range of 300 feet. As an action, you can magically share the Darkvision of this feature with willing creatures you can see within 10 feet of you, up to a number of creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one creature). The shared Darkvision lasts for 1 hour. Once you share it, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest, unless you expend a spell slot of any level to share it again.

features.name: Vigilant Blessing
features.description: The night has taught you to be vigilant. As an action, you give one creature you touch (including possibly yourself) Advantage on the next Initiative roll the creature makes. This benefit ends immediately after the roll or if you use the feature again.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Twilight Sanctuary
features.description: As an action, you present your holy symbol, and a sphere of twilight emanates from you. The sphere is centered on you, has a 30-foot radius, and is filled with dim light. The sphere moves with you, and it lasts for 1 minute or until you are incapacitated or die. Whenever a creature (including you) ends its turn in the sphere, you can grant that creature one of these benefits: give it Temporary Hit Points equal to 1d6 plus your Cleric level, or end one effect on it causing the Charmed or Frightened condition.

features.name: Steps of Night
features.description: You can draw on the mystical power of night to rush with impossible speed. When you are in dim light or darkness, as a Bonus Action, you can magically give yourself a Flying Speed equal to your walking speed for 1 minute. You can use this bonus action a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.description: You gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 Radiant damage to the target. This increases to 2d8 at level 14.

features.name: Twilight Shroud
features.description: The twilight that you summon offers a protective embrace: you and your allies have Half Cover while in the sphere created by your Twilight Sanctuary.

options.name: Option A
options.text: Leather Armor, Shield, Sickle, Druidic Focus (Quarterstaff), Explorer's Pack, Herbalism Kit, and 9 GP

options.name: Option B
options.text: 50 GP

1.name: Spellcasting
1.text: You have learned to cast spells through studying the mystical forces of nature. Cantrips: you know two cantrips of your choice from the Druid spell list (Druidcraft and Produce Flame recommended); you learn another at Druid levels 4 and 10. Spell Slots: the Druid Features table shows how many spell slots you have; you regain all expended slots on a Long Rest. Prepared Spells of Level 1+: you prepare a list of level 1+ Druid spells, starting with four level 1 spells; the number increases as you gain levels, and you can change the list whenever you finish a Long Rest. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability. You can use a Druidic Focus as a Spellcasting Focus.

choices.label: Prepared Spells (from Druid list; count per progression_table)

1.description: You have learned to cast spells through your connection to nature. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability. You can prepare a number of spells equal to your Wisdom modifier plus your Druid level.

1.name: Druidic
1.text: You know Druidic, the secret language of Druids. While learning this ancient tongue, you also unlocked the magic of communicating with animals; you always have the Speak with Animals spell prepared. You can use Druidic to leave hidden messages; you and others who know Druidic automatically spot such a message, and others spot the message's presence with a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check but can't decipher it without magic.
1.description: You know Druidic, the secret language of Druids. You can speak it and use it to leave hidden messages. You and others who know this language automatically spot such a message. Others spot the message's presence with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check but can't decipher it without magic.

1.name: Primal Order
1.text: You have dedicated yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice.

options.name: Magician
options.text: You know one extra cantrip from the Druid spell list. In addition, your mystical connection to nature gives you a bonus to your Intelligence (Arcana or Nature) checks equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum bonus of +1).

options.name: Warden
options.text: Trained for battle, you gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Medium armor.

1.description: You have dedicated yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice: Magician (you know one extra cantrip from the Druid spell list, and Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for Druid spells) or Warden (you gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Medium armor).

2.name: Wild Shape
2.text: The power of nature allows you to assume the form of an animal. As a Bonus Action, you shape-shift into a Beast form that you have learned. You stay in that form for a number of hours equal to half your Druid level or until you use Wild Shape again, have the Incapacitated condition, or die; you can leave the form early as a Bonus Action. You can use Wild Shape twice, regaining one expended use on a Short Rest and all on a Long Rest (more uses at higher levels per the table). Known Forms: you know four Beast forms (Beast stat blocks of CR 1/4 or lower lacking a Fly Speed); known forms and max CR increase per the Beast Shapes table (4 forms/CR 1/4 at L2, 6/CR 1/2 at L4, 8/CR 1 with Fly Speed allowed at L8). While shape-shifted you gain Temp HP equal to your Druid level, your statistics are replaced by the Beast's stat block (retaining your creature type, HP, Hit Point Dice, INT/WIS/CHA, class features, languages, feats, and proficiencies), and you can't cast spells.

actions.name: Wild Shape
actions.effect: Transform into a known Beast form; gain Temp HP equal to Druid level

2.description: The power of nature allows you to assume the form of an animal. As a Bonus Action, you transform into a Beast form of your choice that you have learned for this feature (see Wild Shape Forms). You stay in that form for a number of hours equal to half your Druid level, or until you use Wild Shape again, have the Incapacitated condition, or die. You can revert to your true form as a Bonus Action. While in a form, you retain your personality and ability to speak, and your game statistics are replaced by the Beast's statistics, though you retain your alignment and your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. You regain expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

2.name: Wild Companion
2.text: You can summon a nature spirit that assumes an animal form to aid you. As a Magic action, you can expend a spell slot or a use of Wild Shape to cast the Find Familiar spell without Material components. When you cast the spell in this way, the familiar is Fey and disappears when you finish a Long Rest.

actions.name: Wild Companion
actions.effect: Expend a spell slot or Wild Shape use to cast Find Familiar (Fey familiar, lasts until Long Rest)

3.name: Druid Subclass
3.text: You gain a Druid subclass of your choice. The Circle of the Land, Circle of the Moon, Circle of the Sea, and Circle of the Stars subclasses are detailed in this class's subclasses array.
3.description: You gain a Druid subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Druid levels.

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
4.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Druid levels 8, 12, and 16.
4.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Druid levels 8, 12, 16, and 19.

5.name: Wild Resurgence
5.text: Once on each of your turns, if you have no uses of Wild Shape left, you can give yourself one use by expending a spell slot (no action required). In addition, you can expend one use of Wild Shape (no action required) to give yourself a level 1 spell slot, but you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

6.name: Subclass Feature
6.text: You gain a feature from your Druid subclass.
6.description: You gain a feature from your Druid subclass.

7.name: Elemental Fury
7.text: The might of the elements flows through you. You gain one of the following options of your choice.

options.name: Potent Spellcasting
options.text: Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Druid cantrip.

options.name: Primal Strike
options.text: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon or a Beast form's attack in Wild Shape, you can cause the target to take an extra 1d8 Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage (choose when you hit).

7.description: The might of the elements flows through you. You gain one of the following options of your choice: Potent Spellcasting (add Wisdom modifier to Cantrip damage) or Primal Strike (your attacks in Beast or Humanoid form count as Magical for overcoming resistances, and deal an extra 1d8 damage of a type determined by your environment).

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
8.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.
8.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

10.name: Subclass Feature
10.text: You gain a feature from your Druid subclass.
10.description: You gain a feature from your Druid subclass.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
12.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.
12.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

14.name: Subclass Feature
14.text: You gain a feature from your Druid subclass.
14.description: You gain a feature from your Druid subclass.

15.name: Improved Elemental Fury
15.text: The option you chose for Elemental Fury grows more powerful. Potent Spellcasting: when you cast a Druid cantrip with a range of 10 feet or greater, the spell's range increases by 300 feet. Primal Strike: the extra damage of your Primal Strike increases to 2d8.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
16.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.
16.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

18.name: Beast Spells
18.text: While using Wild Shape, you can cast spells in Beast form, except for any spell that has a Material component with a cost specified or that consumes its Material component.
18.description: You can cast many of your Druid spells in any shape you assume using Wild Shape. You can perform the Somatic and Verbal components of a Druid spell while in a Wild Shape form, but you aren't able to provide Material components.

19.name: Epic Boon
19.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Dimensional Travel is recommended.
19.description: You gain the Epic Boon of Luck feat or another Epic Boon feat of your choice.

20.name: Archdruid
20.text: The vitality of nature constantly blooms within you. Evergreen Wild Shape: whenever you roll Initiative and have no uses of Wild Shape left, you regain one expended use of it. Nature Magician: you can convert uses of Wild Shape into a spell slot (no action required); choose a number of unexpended uses of Wild Shape and convert them into a single spell slot, with each use contributing 2 spell levels. Longevity: the primal magic you wield causes you to age more slowly; for every 10 years that pass, your body ages only 1 year.
20.description: The vitality of nature constantly blooms within you, granting you the following benefits: Evergreen Wild Shape (whenever you roll Initiative and have no uses of Wild Shape remaining, you regain one use of it), Nature Magician (you can convert expended spell slots into Wild Shape uses; as a Bonus Action, you lose one unexpended spell slot and regain one expended use of Wild Shape), Longevity (the primal magic you channel causes you to age slowly; for every 10 years that pass, your body ages only 1 year).

subclasses.name: Circle of the Land
subclasses.tagline: Celebrate Connection to the Natural World
subclasses.description: The Circle of the Land comprises mystics and sages who safeguard ancient knowledge and rites, meeting within sacred circles of trees or standing stones.

3.name: Circle of the Land Spells
3.text: Whenever you finish a Long Rest, choose one type of land: arid, polar, temperate, or tropical. Consult the corresponding table; you have the spells listed for your Druid level and lower prepared. ARID: 3 Blur/Burning Hands/Fire Bolt, 5 Fireball, 7 Blight, 9 Wall of Stone. POLAR: 3 Fog Cloud/Hold Person/Ray of Frost, 5 Sleet Storm, 7 Ice Storm, 9 Cone of Cold. TEMPERATE: 3 Misty Step/Shocking Grasp/Sleep, 5 Lightning Bolt, 7 Freedom of Movement, 9 Tree Stride. TROPICAL: 3 Acid Splash/Ray of Sickness/Web, 5 Stinking Cloud, 7 Polymorph, 9 Insect Plague.

options.name: Arid Land
options.text: Lvl 3: Blur, Burning Hands, Fire Bolt. Lvl 5: Fireball. Lvl 7: Blight. Lvl 9: Wall of Stone.

options.name: Polar Land
options.text: Lvl 3: Fog Cloud, Hold Person, Ray of Frost. Lvl 5: Sleet Storm. Lvl 7: Ice Storm. Lvl 9: Cone of Cold.

options.name: Temperate Land
options.text: Lvl 3: Misty Step, Shocking Grasp, Sleep. Lvl 5: Lightning Bolt. Lvl 7: Freedom of Movement. Lvl 9: Tree Stride.

options.name: Tropical Land
options.text: Lvl 3: Acid Splash, Ray of Sickness, Web. Lvl 5: Stinking Cloud. Lvl 7: Polymorph. Lvl 9: Insect Plague.

3.name: Land's Aid
3.text: As a Magic action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape and choose a point within 60 feet of yourself. Vitality-giving flowers and life-draining thorns appear in a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point. Each creature of your choice in the Sphere must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 2d6 Necrotic damage on a failed save or half on a success. One creature of your choice in that area regains 2d6 Hit Points. The damage and healing increase by 1d6 at Druid levels 10 (3d6) and 14 (4d6).

actions.name: Land's Aid
actions.effect: CON save, 2d6 Necrotic (half on save) in a 10-ft Sphere; one chosen creature regains 2d6 HP; scales 3d6@10, 4d6@14

6.name: Natural Recovery
6.text: You can cast one of the level 1+ spells that you have prepared from your Circle Spells feature without expending a spell slot, and you must finish a Long Rest before you do so again. In addition, when you finish a Short Rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover; the combined level may equal at most half your Druid level (round up), none of them level 6+. Once you recover spell slots this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

10.name: Nature's Ward
10.text: You are immune to the Poisoned condition, and you have Resistance to a damage type associated with your current land choice in the Circle Spells feature: Arid - Fire, Polar - Cold, Temperate - Lightning, Tropical - Poison.

14.name: Nature's Sanctuary
14.text: As a Magic action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape and cause spectral trees and vines to appear in a 15-foot Cube on the ground within 120 feet of yourself. They last for 1 minute or until you have the Incapacitated condition or die. You and your allies have Half Cover while in that area, and your allies gain the current Resistance of your Nature's Ward while there. As a Bonus Action, you can move the Cube up to 60 feet to ground within 120 feet of yourself.

features.name: Circle Spells
features.description: Your mystical connection to the land infuses you with the ability to cast certain spells. Choose one of the following lands and gain the associated spells, which are always prepared: Arid (Blur, Burning Hands, Fire Bolt, Fireball, Wall of Sand), Arctic (Cone of Cold, Fog Cloud, Hold Person, Ice Storm, Sleet Storm), Coast (Mirror Image, Misty Step, Shapechange, Thunderwave, Water Walk), Forest (Call Lightning, Invisibility, Misty Step, Phantasmal Force, Plant Growth), Grassland (Daylight, Entangle, Haste, Misty Step, Short-ranged Thunderwave), Mountain (Earth Tremor, Meld into Stone, Passwall, Spike Growth, Stone Shape), Swamp (Darkness, Melf's Acid Arrow, Stinking Cloud, Vampiric Touch, Water Breathing), Underdark (Blur, Gaseous Form, Greater Invisibility, Meld into Stone, Sleet Storm).

features.name: Land's Aid
features.description: As a Magic action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape and choose a point within 60 feet of yourself. Vitality-laden magic radiates from that point in a 10-foot-radius sphere for 1 minute. For the duration, you and your allies in the sphere gain Advantage on Constitution saving throws, and any creature in the sphere that spends Hit Dice during a Short Rest can reroll each die once.

features.name: Natural Recovery
features.description: You can cast one of your Circle Spells without expending a spell slot. You regain this ability when you finish a Long Rest. In addition, once per Long Rest when you finish a Short Rest, you can recover a number of expended Spell Slots of a combined level up to half your Druid level (rounded up).

features.name: Nature's Ward
features.description: You are immune to the Frightened and Poisoned conditions. You also have resistance to a damage type associated with your land: Arid (fire), Arctic (cold), Coast (lightning), Forest (poison), Grassland (lightning), Mountain (thunder), Swamp (acid), Underdark (necrotic).

features.name: Nature's Sanctuary
features.description: As a Magic action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape to make yourself immune to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage for 10 minutes or until you use Wild Shape again. While this immunity is active, once per turn when a creature hits you with a weapon attack, the creature takes force damage equal to your Wisdom modifier.

subclasses.name: Circle of the Moon
subclasses.tagline: Adopt Animal Forms to Guard the Wilds
subclasses.description: Druids of the Circle of the Moon draw on lunar magic to transform themselves, prowling as great cats, soaring as eagles, or crashing through undergrowth as bears.

3.name: Circle Forms
3.text: You can channel lunar magic when you assume a Wild Shape form. Challenge Rating: the maximum Challenge Rating for the form equals your Druid level divided by 3 (round down). Armor Class: until you leave the form, your AC equals 13 plus your Wisdom modifier if that total is higher than the Beast's AC. Temporary Hit Points: you gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to three times your Druid level.

3.name: Circle of the Moon Spells
3.text: When you reach the listed Druid levels, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

6.name: Improved Circle Forms
6.text: While in a Wild Shape form, you gain the following benefits. Lunar Radiance: each of your attacks in a Wild Shape form can deal its normal damage type or Radiant damage (your choice each time you hit). Increased Toughness: you can add your Wisdom modifier to your Constitution saving throws.

10.name: Moonlight Step
10.text: You magically transport yourself, reappearing amid a burst of moonlight. As a Bonus Action, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, and you have Advantage on the next attack roll you make before the end of this turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), regaining all uses on a Long Rest, or by expending a level 2+ spell slot for each use you want to restore.

actions.name: Moonlight Step
actions.effect: Teleport 30 ft; Advantage on your next attack this turn

14.name: Lunar Form
14.text: The power of the moon suffuses you. Improved Lunar Radiance: once per turn, you can deal an extra 2d10 Radiant damage to a target you hit with a Wild Shape form's attack. Shared Moonlight: whenever you use Moonlight Step, you can also teleport one willing creature within 10 feet of you to an unoccupied space you can see within 10 feet of your destination space.

features.name: Combat Wild Shape
features.description: You gain the ability to use Wild Shape as a Bonus Action. Additionally, while you are in a Wild Shape form, you can use a Bonus Action to expend one spell slot to regain 1d8 hit points per level of the spell slot expended.

features.name: Circle Forms
features.description: You can use Wild Shape to transform into a beast with a maximum CR of 1 (instead of 1/4). Starting at 6th level, the CR maximum equals half your Druid level. You can also transform into elementals (Air, Earth, Fire, Water) when you reach 10th level.

features.name: Elemental Wild Shape
features.description: You can expend two uses of Wild Shape at the same time to transform into an air, earth, fire, or water elemental.

features.name: Thousand Forms
features.description: You have learned to use magic to alter your physical form in more subtle ways. You can cast the Alter Self spell at will.

features.name: Beastspell
features.description: While transformed by Wild Shape, you can cast spells in beast form. You can perform the somatic and verbal components of a Druid spell while in beast form, but you aren't able to provide material components.

subclasses.name: Circle of the Sea
subclasses.tagline: Become One with Tides and Storms
subclasses.description: Druids of the Circle of the Sea draw on the tempestuous forces of oceans and storms, attuning themselves to the ebb and flow of the tides.

3.name: Circle of the Sea Spells
3.text: When you reach the listed Druid levels, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

3.name: Wrath of the Sea
3.text: As a Bonus Action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape to manifest a 5-foot Emanation that takes the form of ocean spray surrounding you for 10 minutes (ends early if dismissed, manifested again, or you have the Incapacitated condition). When you manifest the Emanation and as a Bonus Action on subsequent turns, you can choose another creature you can see in the Emanation; it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or take Cold damage (roll a number of d6s equal to your Wisdom modifier, minimum one) and, if Large or smaller, be pushed up to 15 feet away from you.

actions.name: Wrath of the Sea
actions.effect: CON save or Cold damage (WIS-mod d6s) + push 15 ft

6.name: Aquatic Affinity
6.text: The size of the Emanation created by your Wrath of the Sea increases to 10 feet. In addition, you gain a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.

10.name: Stormborn
10.text: Your Wrath of the Sea confers two more benefits while active. Flight: you gain a Fly Speed equal to your Speed. Resistance: you have Resistance to Cold, Lightning, and Thunder damage.

14.name: Oceanic Gift
14.text: Instead of manifesting the Emanation of Wrath of the Sea around yourself, you can manifest it around one willing creature within 60 feet of yourself; that creature gains all the benefits of the Emanation and uses your spell save DC and Wisdom modifier for it. In addition, you can manifest the Emanation around both the other creature and yourself if you expend two uses of your Wild Shape instead of one.

features.name: Wrath of the Sea
features.description: As a Bonus Action, you can expend a use of Wild Shape to manifest a 5-foot aura of ocean water that lasts for 10 minutes. It ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), are Incapacitated, or use this feature again. When the aura appears, choose a number of creatures you can see within 10 feet equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). Each of them must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or take Cold damage and be pushed up to 15 feet away. The damage equals 2d6 + your Wisdom modifier. While the aura lasts, you can take this action again on each of your turns.

features.name: Sea Spells
features.description: Your connection to the sea grants you the following always-prepared spells: 3rd (Fog Cloud, Thunderwave), 5th (Gust of Wind, Shatter), 9th (Lightning Bolt, Water Breathing), 13th (Control Water, Watery Sphere), 17th (Conjure Elemental, Hold Monster).

features.name: Aquatic Affinity
features.description: The size of the aura from Wrath of the Sea increases to 10 feet. Additionally, you gain a Swim Speed equal to your Speed and can breathe underwater.

features.name: Stormborn
features.description: Your Wrath of the Sea aura now also grants you and allies in it resistance to Cold and Lightning damage. In addition, being underwater doesn't impose disadvantage on your attack rolls or ranged attack rolls against creatures underwater.

features.name: Oceanic Gift
features.description: Instead of manifesting the aura around yourself, you can manifest it around one willing creature within 60 feet of yourself. That creature gains all the benefits of the aura and you can activate the aura's action for that creature, not yourself. A creature can receive this benefit for up to 10 minutes per day.

subclasses.name: Circle of the Stars
subclasses.tagline: Harness Secrets Hidden in Constellations
subclasses.description: The Circle of the Stars has tracked heavenly patterns since time immemorial, seeking to harness the powers of the cosmos hidden amid the constellations.

3.name: Star Map
3.text: You've created a star chart. It is a Tiny object you can use as a Spellcasting Focus for your Druid spells. While holding the map, you have the Guidance and Guiding Bolt spells prepared, and you can cast Guiding Bolt without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), regaining all uses on a Long Rest. If you lose the map, you can perform a 1-hour ceremony during a Short or Long Rest to create a replacement.

3.name: Starry Form
3.text: As a Bonus Action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape feature to take on a starry form rather than shape-shifting. While in your starry form you retain your game statistics; your body becomes luminous, sheds Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet, and the form lasts 10 minutes (ends early if dismissed, Incapacitated, or used again). Choose a constellation: Archer - when you activate the form and as a Bonus Action on subsequent turns, make a ranged spell attack for 1d8 + Wisdom modifier Radiant damage to a creature within 60 ft. Chalice - whenever you cast a spell with a spell slot that restores Hit Points to a creature, you or another creature within 30 ft regains 1d8 + Wisdom modifier HP. Dragon - when you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check or a Constitution save to maintain Concentration, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

choices.label: Constellation (choose when you assume Starry Form)

options.name: Archer
options.text: Bonus Action ranged spell attack for 1d8 + WIS Radiant damage to a creature within 60 ft.

options.name: Chalice
options.text: When you cast a healing spell with a slot, you or a creature within 30 ft regains 1d8 + WIS HP.

options.name: Dragon
options.text: Treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10 on INT/WIS checks and CON saves to maintain Concentration.

actions.name: Starry Form
actions.effect: Expend a Wild Shape use to enter a 10-min starry form with a chosen constellation

6.name: Cosmic Omen
6.text: Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can consult your Star Map and roll a die. Until your next Long Rest you gain a special Reaction: Weal (even) - whenever a creature within 30 feet is about to make a D20 Test, roll 1d6 and add it to the total. Woe (odd) - whenever a creature within 30 feet is about to make a D20 Test, roll 1d6 and subtract it from the total. You can use this Reaction a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), regaining all uses on a Long Rest.

actions.name: Cosmic Omen
actions.effect: Add (Weal) or subtract (Woe) 1d6 on a creature's D20 Test

10.name: Twinkling Constellations
10.text: The constellations of your Starry Form improve. The 1d8 of the Archer and the Chalice becomes 2d8, and while the Dragon is active you have a Fly Speed of 20 feet and can hover. Moreover, at the start of each of your turns while in your Starry Form, you can change which constellation glimmers on your body.

14.name: Full of Stars
14.text: While in your Starry Form, you become partially incorporeal, giving you Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

features.name: Star Map
features.description: You've created a star chart as part of your studies. It is a Tiny object and can serve as a spellcasting focus for your Druid spells. While holding it, you have the Guidance and Guiding Bolt spells always prepared; they don't count against the number of spells you can prepare. You can cast Guiding Bolt without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses on a Long Rest.

features.name: Starry Form
features.description: When you use Wild Shape, you can expend a use to take on a starry form instead of transforming into a beast. In this form, you shed bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet. Choose one of the following constellations for benefits: Archer (bonus action ranged spell attack, 1d8+Wis radiant), Chalice (healing spells also restore 1d8+Wis HP to you), Dragon (concentration gives advantage on saves, and resistance to one damage type that caused a failed save).

features.name: Cosmic Omen
features.description: You learn to use your star map to portend the future. When you finish a Long Rest, roll a die. Until you finish your next Long Rest, you can use a reaction when a creature within 30 feet makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw to add or subtract 1d6 (Weal if even, Woe if odd). Uses equal your proficiency bonus, regaining on Long Rest.

features.name: Twinkling Constellations
features.description: The constellations of your Starry Form improve. The 1d8 of the Archer and Chalice forms become 2d8. While in Starry Form, you can use a Bonus Action to teleport up to 20 feet.

features.name: Full of Stars
features.description: While in Starry Form, you become partially incorporeal, giving you resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

subclasses.name: Circle of Dreams
subclasses.edition_note: Originally published for 2014 rules in Xanathar's Guide to Everything; feature levels (2/6/10/14) are as printed in that book.
subclasses.tagline: Fill the World with Dreamy Wonder
subclasses.description: Druids who are members of the Circle of Dreams hail from regions that have strong ties to the Feywild and its dreamlike realms. These druids seek to fill the world with dreamy wonder; their magic mends wounds and brings joy to downcast hearts.

2.name: Balm of the Summer Court
2.text: You become imbued with the blessings of the Summer Court. You have a pool of fey energy represented by a number of d6s equal to your druid level. As a bonus action, you can choose one creature you can see within 120 feet of you and spend a number of those dice equal to half your druid level or less. Roll the spent dice and add them together; the target regains a number of hit points equal to the total, and also gains 1 temporary hit point per die spent. You regain all expended dice when you finish a long rest.

choices.label: Balm of the Summer Court pool of d6s (= druid level)

6.name: Hearth of Moonlight and Shadow
6.text: Home can be wherever you are. During a short or long rest, you can invoke the shadowy power of the Gloaming Court to help guard your respite. At the start of the rest, you touch a point in space, and an invisible, 30-foot-radius sphere of magic appears centered on that point (total cover blocks the sphere). While within the sphere, you and your allies gain a +5 bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) and Wisdom (Perception) checks, and any light from open flames in the sphere isn't visible outside it. The sphere vanishes at the end of the rest or when you leave the sphere.

10.name: Hidden Paths
10.text: You can use the hidden, magical pathways that some fey use to traverse space in the blink of an eye. As a bonus action on your turn, you can teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Alternatively, you can use your action to teleport one willing creature you touch up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

choices.label: Hidden Paths uses (= Wisdom modifier, min 1)

14.name: Walker in Dreams
14.text: The magic of the Feywild grants you the ability to travel mentally or physically through dreamlands. When you finish a short rest, you can cast one of the following spells, without expending a spell slot or requiring material components: Dream (with you as the messenger), Scrying, or Teleportation Circle. This use of Teleportation Circle is special: rather than opening a portal to a permanent teleportation circle, it opens a portal to the last location where you finished a long rest on your current plane of existence (if you haven't taken a long rest on your current plane, the spell fails but isn't wasted). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

features.name: Balm of the Summer Court
features.description: You become imbued with the blessings of the Summer Court. You are a font of energy that offers respite from injuries. You have a pool of fey energy represented by a number of d6s equal to your Druid level. As a Bonus Action, you can choose one creature you can see within 120 feet and spend a number of those dice equal to half your Druid level or less. Roll the spent dice and add them together. The target regains a number of hit points equal to the total, and gains 1 temporary hit point per die spent. You regain all expended dice when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Hearth of Moonlight and Shadow
features.description: Home can be wherever you are. During a Short or Long Rest, you can invoke the shadowy power of the Gleaming Court to ward your campsite. At the start of the rest, you touch a point in space, and an invisible, 30-foot-radius sphere of magic appears centered on that point. Total cover blocks the sphere. While within the sphere, you and your allies gain a +5 bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) and Wisdom (Perception) checks and any light from open flames in the sphere (a campfire, torches, or the like) isn't visible outside it. The sphere vanishes at the end of the rest or when you leave the sphere.

features.name: Hidden Paths
features.description: You can use the hidden, magical pathways that some fey use to traverse space in the blink of an eye. As a Bonus Action on your turn, you can teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Alternatively, you can use your action to teleport one willing creature you touch up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Walker in Dreams
features.description: The magic of the Feywild grants you the ability to travel mentally or physically through dreamscapes. When you finish a Short Rest, you can cast Scrying, Dream, or Teleportation Circle (without material components) without expending a spell slot. The target of the Scrying spell must be someone you know. When you cast Teleportation Circle using this feature, you can instead open a portal to a place the target creature considers a home.

subclasses.name: Circle of the Shepherd
subclasses.edition_note: Originally published for 2014 rules in Xanathar's Guide to Everything; feature levels (2/6/10/14) are as printed in that book.
subclasses.tagline: Commune with the Spirits of Nature
subclasses.description: Druids of the Circle of the Shepherd commune with the spirits of nature, especially the spirits of beasts and the fey, and call to those spirits for aid. Shepherds focus on protecting animals and fey creatures that have difficulty defending themselves.

2.name: Speech of the Woods
2.text: You gain the ability to converse with beasts and many fey. You learn to speak, read, and write Sylvan. In addition, beasts can understand your speech, and you gain the ability to decipher their noises and motions. Most beasts lack the intelligence to convey or understand sophisticated concepts, but a friendly beast could relay what it has seen or heard in the recent past. This ability doesn't grant you friendship with beasts, though you can combine it with gifts to curry favor with them as you would with any NPC.

2.name: Spirit Totem
2.text: You can call forth nature spirits to influence the world around you. As a bonus action, you can magically summon an incorporeal spirit to a point you can see within 60 feet of you. The spirit creates an aura in a 30-foot radius around that point; it counts as neither a creature nor an object, though it has the spectral appearance of the creature it represents. As a bonus action, you can move the spirit up to 60 feet to a point you can see. The spirit persists for 1 minute or until you're incapacitated. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest. Bear Spirit: Each creature of your choice in the aura when the spirit appears gains temporary hit points equal to 5 + your druid level; in addition, you and your allies gain advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws while in the aura. Hawk Spirit: When a creature makes an attack roll against a target in the spirit's aura, you can use your reaction to grant advantage to that attack roll; in addition, you and your allies have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks while in the aura.
