Martial Arts Die - you can roll 1d6 in place of the normal damage of your Unarmed Strike or Monk weapons; this die changes as you gain levels (per the Martial Arts column). Dexterous Attacks - you can use your Dexterity modifier instead of Strength for attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes and Monk weapons, and for the save DC of Grapple/Shove.

actions.name: Unarmed Strike (Bonus Action)
actions.effect: Make an Unarmed Strike (Martial Arts die damage, DEX-based)

1.description: Your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use unarmed strikes and monk weapons, which are Simple Melee weapons and Martial Melee weapons with the Light property. You gain the following benefits while you are unarmed or wielding only monk weapons and you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield: Bonus Unarmed Strike (after you take the Attack action, you can make one Unarmed Strike as a Bonus Action), Dexterous Attacks (you can use DEX instead of STR for the attack and damage rolls of your unarmed strikes and monk weapons), Martial Arts Die (your Unarmed Strikes use a d6 die; this increases as you gain Monk levels).

1.name: Unarmored Defense
1.text: While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Wisdom modifiers.
1.description: While you aren't wearing any armor or wielding a Shield, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity modifier plus your Wisdom modifier.

2.name: Monk's Focus
2.text: Your focus and martial training allow you to harness a well of extraordinary energy represented by Focus Points (your Monk level determines how many, per the Focus Points column). When you expend a Focus Point it is unavailable until you finish a Short or Long Rest. Save DC for Focus features equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and Proficiency Bonus. You start knowing three features: Flurry of Blows - expend 1 Focus Point to make two Unarmed Strikes as a Bonus Action. Patient Defense - take the Disengage action as a Bonus Action, or expend 1 Focus Point to take both Disengage and Dodge as a Bonus Action. Step of the Wind - take the Dash action as a Bonus Action, or expend 1 Focus Point to take both Disengage and Dash as a Bonus Action and double your jump distance for the turn.

actions.name: Flurry of Blows
actions.effect: Expend 1 Focus Point: make two Unarmed Strikes (three at level 10)

actions.name: Patient Defense
actions.effect: Disengage; or expend 1 Focus Point for Disengage + Dodge

actions.name: Step of the Wind
actions.effect: Dash; or expend 1 Focus Point for Disengage + Dash + double jump

2.description: Your focus and martial training allow you to harness a well of extraordinary energy within yourself. This energy is represented by Focus Points. Your Monk level determines the number of points you have (equal to your Monk level). You can spend these points to fuel certain Monk features. You regain all expended Focus Points when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

2.name: Unarmored Movement
2.text: Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield. This bonus increases at higher Monk levels (per the Unarmored Movement column).

choices.label: Speed bonus while unarmored (scales per progression_table)

2.description: Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield. This bonus increases when you reach certain Monk levels (15 ft at level 6, 20 ft at level 10, 25 ft at level 14, 30 ft at level 18).

2.name: Uncanny Metabolism
2.text: When you roll Initiative, you can regain all expended Focus Points. When you do so, roll your Martial Arts die and regain a number of Hit Points equal to your Monk level plus the number rolled. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

3.name: Deflect Attacks
3.text: When an attack roll hits you and its damage includes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce the attack's total damage against you by 1d10 plus your Dexterity modifier and Monk level. If you reduce the damage to 0, you can expend 1 Focus Point to redirect some of the attack's force: choose a creature within 5 feet (melee) or within 60 feet not behind Total Cover (ranged); that creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die plus your Dexterity modifier, of the same type dealt by the attack.

actions.name: Deflect Attacks
actions.effect: Reduce attack damage by 1d10 + DEX + Monk level; optionally redirect

3.description: When an attack roll hits you and its damage includes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you can use your Reaction to reduce that damage. The reduction equals 1d10 plus your Dexterity modifier plus your Monk level. If you reduce the damage to 0, you can expend 1 Focus Point and redirect it; you catch the missile and can spend the Focus Point to make a Ranged Attack (range 20/60 ft) as part of the same Reaction, using your Monk attack modifier.

3.name: Monk Subclass
3.text: You gain a Monk subclass of your choice. The Warrior of Mercy, Warrior of Shadow, Warrior of the Elements, and Warrior of the Open Hand subclasses are detailed in this class's subclasses array.
3.description: You gain a Monk subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Monk levels.

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
4.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Monk levels 8, 12, and 16.
4.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Monk levels 8, 12, 16, and 19.

4.name: Slow Fall
4.text: You can take a Reaction when you fall to reduce any damage you take from the fall by an amount equal to five times your Monk level.
4.description: You can use your Reaction when you fall to reduce any damage you take from falling by an amount equal to five times your Monk level.

5.name: Extra Attack
5.text: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
5.description: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

5.name: Stunning Strike
5.text: Once per turn when you hit a creature with a Monk weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can expend 1 Focus Point to attempt a stunning strike. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the Stunned condition until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the target's Speed is halved until the start of your next turn, and the next attack roll made against it before then has Advantage.
5.description: Upgraded at this level — if the target succeeds on the CON save, the target's Speed is halved until the start of your next turn.

6.name: Empowered Strikes
6.text: Whenever you deal damage with your Unarmed Strike, it can deal your choice of Force damage or its normal damage type.
6.description: Whenever you deal damage with your Unarmed Strike, it can deal your choice of Force damage or its normal damage type.

6.name: Subclass Feature
6.text: You gain a feature from your Monk subclass.
6.description: You gain a feature from your Monk subclass.

7.name: Evasion
7.text: When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. You don't benefit from this feature if you have the Incapacitated condition.
7.description: When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
8.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.
8.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

9.name: Acrobatic Movement
9.text: While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the movement.
9.description: While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the movement.

10.name: Heightened Focus
10.text: Your Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind gain benefits. Flurry of Blows: you can expend 1 Focus Point to use Flurry of Blows and make three Unarmed Strikes instead of two. Patient Defense: when you expend a Focus Point to use Patient Defense, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die. Step of the Wind: when you expend a Focus Point to use Step of the Wind, you can choose a willing Large-or-smaller creature within 5 feet of yourself and move it with you until the end of your turn without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
10.description: Your Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind gain the following benefits. Flurry of Blows: you can spend 1 Focus Point to make two Unarmed Strikes as a Bonus Action; each target you hit can also be pushed 5 feet away from you, forced Prone, or slowed (its Speed halved until the start of its next turn). Patient Defense: costs 1 Focus Point; you take the Dodge action as a Bonus Action and gain +1 AC until start of your next turn. Step of the Wind: you can expend 1 Focus Point to Dash/Disengage as a Bonus Action and can bring one willing creature within 5 ft of you along.

10.name: Self-Restoration
10.text: Through sheer force of will, you can remove one of the following conditions from yourself at the end of each of your turns: Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned. In addition, forgoing food and drink doesn't give you levels of Exhaustion.
10.description: Through sheer force of will, you can remove debilitating effects from yourself. At the end of each of your turns, you can end one effect on yourself causing any of the following conditions: Blinded, Deafened, or Poisoned.

11.name: Subclass Feature
11.text: You gain a feature from your Monk subclass.
11.description: You gain a feature from your Monk subclass.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
12.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.
12.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

13.name: Deflect Energy
13.text: You can now use your Deflect Attacks feature against attacks that deal any damage type, not just Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing.
13.description: You can now use Deflect Attacks against attacks that deal any damage type, not just Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing.

14.name: Disciplined Survivor
14.text: Your physical and mental discipline grant you proficiency in all saving throws. Additionally, whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can expend 1 Focus Point to reroll it, and you must use the new roll.
14.description: Your physical and mental discipline grant you proficiency in all saving throws. Additionally, whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can spend 1 Focus Point to reroll it and take the second result.

15.name: Perfect Focus
15.text: When you roll Initiative and don't use Uncanny Metabolism, you regain expended Focus Points until you have 4 if you have 3 or fewer.
15.description: When you roll Initiative and have no Focus Points remaining, you regain Focus Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
16.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.
16.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

17.name: Subclass Feature
17.text: You gain a feature from your Monk subclass.
17.description: You gain a feature from your Monk subclass.

18.name: Superior Defense
18.text: At the start of your turn, you can expend 3 Focus Points to bolster yourself against harm for 1 minute or until you have the Incapacitated condition. During that time, you have Resistance to all damage except Force damage.

19.name: Epic Boon
19.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Irresistible Offense is recommended.
19.description: You gain the Epic Boon of Irresistible Offense feat or another Epic Boon feat of your choice.

20.name: Body and Mind
20.text: You have developed your body and mind to new heights. Your Dexterity and Wisdom scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.
20.description: You have perfected your body and mind to new heights. Your Dexterity and Wisdom scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

subclasses.name: Warrior of Mercy
subclasses.tagline: Manipulate Forces of Life and Death
subclasses.description: Warriors of Mercy manipulate the life force of others. These Monks are wandering physicians who can bring a swift end to their enemies, often wearing masks as faceless bringers of life and death.

3.name: Hand of Harm
3.text: Once per turn when you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike and deal damage, you can expend 1 Focus Point to deal extra Necrotic damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die plus your Wisdom modifier.

3.name: Hand of Healing
3.text: As a Magic action, you can expend 1 Focus Point to touch a creature and restore a number of Hit Points equal to a roll of your Martial Arts die plus your Wisdom modifier. When you use your Flurry of Blows, you can replace one of the Unarmed Strikes with a use of this feature without expending a Focus Point for the healing.

actions.name: Hand of Healing
actions.effect: Expend 1 Focus Point: heal Martial Arts die + WIS modifier

3.name: Implements of Mercy
3.text: You gain proficiency in the Insight and Medicine skills and proficiency with the Herbalism Kit.

6.name: Physician's Touch
6.text: Your Hand of Harm and Hand of Healing improve. Hand of Harm: when you use it on a creature, you can also give that creature the Poisoned condition until the end of your next turn. Hand of Healing: when you use it, you can also end one of the following conditions on the creature you heal: Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, or Stunned.

11.name: Flurry of Healing and Harm
11.text: When you use Flurry of Blows, you can replace each of the Unarmed Strikes with a use of Hand of Healing without expending Focus Points for the healing. In addition, when you make an Unarmed Strike with Flurry of Blows and deal damage, you can use Hand of Harm with that strike without expending a Focus Point for Hand of Harm (still only once per turn).

17.name: Hand of Ultimate Mercy
17.text: As a Magic action, you can touch the corpse of a creature that died within the past 24 hours and expend 5 Focus Points. The creature returns to life with a number of Hit Points equal to 4d10 plus your Wisdom modifier; if it died with any of the following conditions, it revives with them removed: Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, and Stunned. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

actions.name: Hand of Ultimate Mercy
actions.effect: Expend 5 Focus Points: revive a corpse (dead <=24h) with 4d10 + WIS HP

features.name: Implements of Mercy
features.description: You gain proficiency in the Insight and Medicine skills, and proficiency with the Herbalism Kit. You also gain a special mask that you can don as a Bonus Action. While wearing the mask, creatures that can see you have disadvantage on saving throws against your Flurry of Blows attacks that use Hand of Harm or Hand of Healing.

features.name: Hand of Harm
features.description: Once per turn when you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, you can spend 1 Focus Point to deal extra Necrotic damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die plus your Wisdom modifier. You can also subject the target to the Poisoned condition until the end of your next turn.

features.name: Hand of Healing
features.description: As a Magic action, you can spend 1 Focus Point to touch a creature and restore a number of Hit Points equal to a roll of your Martial Arts die plus your Wisdom modifier. When you use Flurry of Blows, you can replace one of the Unarmed Strikes with a use of this feature without spending a Focus Point for the healing.

features.name: Physician's Touch
features.description: Your Hand of Harm also afflicts the target with one disease or condition from the following list: Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, or Stunned until the end of your next turn. Your Hand of Healing can also end one disease affecting the target or remove one condition (Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, or Stunned).

features.name: Flurry of Healing and Harm
features.description: When you use Flurry of Blows, you can replace each of the Unarmed Strikes with a use of Hand of Healing without spending additional Focus Points. In addition, when you make an Unarmed Strike with Flurry of Blows, you can use Hand of Harm with that strike without spending additional Focus Points. You can still use Hand of Harm only once per turn.

features.name: Hand of Ultimate Mercy
features.description: Your mastery of life energy opens the door to the ultimate mercy. As a Magic action, you can touch the corpse of a creature that died within the past 24 hours and expend 5 Focus Points. The creature then returns to life, regaining a number of Hit Points equal to 4d10 + your Wisdom modifier. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Warrior of Shadow
subclasses.tagline: Harness Shadow Power for Stealth and Subterfuge
subclasses.description: Warriors of Shadow practice stealth and subterfuge, harnessing the power of the Shadowfell. They are at home in darkness, able to draw gloom around themselves to hide.

3.name: Shadow Arts
3.text: You have learned to draw on the power of the Shadowfell. Darkness: you can expend 1 Focus Point to cast the Darkness spell without spell components; you can see within the spell's area when you cast it this way, and while it persists you can move its area to a space within 60 feet of yourself at the start of each of your turns. Darkvision: you gain Darkvision with a range of 60 feet (if you already have it, its range increases by 60 feet). Shadowy Figments: you know the Minor Illusion spell; Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it.

6.name: Shadow Step
6.text: While entirely within Dim Light or Darkness, you can use a Bonus Action to teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in Dim Light or Darkness. You then have Advantage on the next melee attack you make before the end of the current turn.

actions.name: Shadow Step
actions.effect: Teleport between areas of Dim Light/Darkness; Advantage on next melee attack

11.name: Improved Shadow Step
11.text: When you use your Shadow Step, you can expend 1 Focus Point to remove the requirement that you must start and end in Dim Light or Darkness for that use. As part of this Bonus Action, you can make an Unarmed Strike immediately after you teleport.

17.name: Cloak of Shadows
17.text: As a Magic action while entirely within Dim Light or Darkness, you can expend 3 Focus Points to shroud yourself with shadows for 1 minute, until you have the Incapacitated condition, or until you end your turn in Bright Light. While shrouded: Invisibility - you have the Invisible condition. Partially Incorporeal - you can move through occupied spaces as if they were Difficult Terrain. Shadow Flurry - you can use your Flurry of Blows without expending any Focus Points.

actions.name: Cloak of Shadows
actions.effect: Expend 3 Focus Points: gain Invisible, partial incorporeality, and free Flurry of Blows for 1 min

features.name: Shadow Arts
features.description: You can spend 1 Focus Point to cast Darkness, Darkvision, Pass without Trace, or Silence without requiring spell components. You also know the Minor Illusion cantrip and can spend 1 Focus Point to cast it without material components.

features.name: Shadow Step
features.description: When you are in dim light or darkness, as a Bonus Action you can teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in dim light or darkness. You then have advantage on the first melee attack you make before the end of the turn.

features.name: Cloak of Shadows
features.description: While in dim light or darkness, you can use your action to become Invisible. You remain Invisible until you make an attack, cast a spell, or are in an area of bright light.

features.name: Opportunist
features.description: You can exploit a creature's momentary distraction when it is hit by an attack. Whenever a creature within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack made by a creature other than you, you can use your Reaction to make a melee attack against that creature.

subclasses.name: Warrior of the Elements
subclasses.tagline: Wield Strikes and Bursts of Elemental Power
subclasses.description: Warriors of the Elements tap into the power of the Elemental Planes, momentarily taming the energy of the Elemental Chaos to empower themselves in and out of battle.

3.name: Elemental Attunement
3.text: At the start of your turn, you can expend 1 Focus Point to imbue yourself with elemental energy for 10 minutes or until you have the Incapacitated condition. While active: Reach - when you make an Unarmed Strike, your reach is 10 feet greater than normal. Elemental Strikes - whenever you hit with your Unarmed Strike, you can cause it to deal your choice of Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage; when you deal one of these types, you can also force the target to make a Strength saving throw, and on a failed save move it up to 10 feet toward or away from you.

3.name: Manipulate Elements
3.text: You know the Elementalism spell. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it.

6.name: Elemental Burst
6.text: As a Magic action, you can expend 2 Focus Points to cause elemental energy to burst in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point within 120 feet of yourself. Choose a damage type: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder. Each creature in the Sphere must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking damage of the chosen type equal to three rolls of your Martial Arts die on a failed save or half as much on a success.

actions.name: Elemental Burst
actions.effect: Expend 2 Focus Points: DEX save, 3x Martial Arts die elemental damage in a 20-ft Sphere

11.name: Stride of the Elements
11.text: While your Elemental Attunement is active, you also have a Fly Speed and a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.

17.name: Elemental Epitome
17.text: While your Elemental Attunement is active, you gain benefits. Damage Resistance: you gain Resistance to one of Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder of your choice; at the start of each of your turns you can change this choice. Destructive Stride: when you use Step of the Wind, your Speed increases by 20 feet until the end of the turn, and any creature of your choice takes damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die when you enter a space within 5 feet of it (chosen type; once per turn per creature). Empowered Strikes: once on each of your turns, you can deal extra damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die when you hit with an Unarmed Strike.

features.name: Elemental Attunement
features.description: At the start of your turn, you can spend 1 Focus Point (no action required) to imbue yourself with elemental energy. For 10 minutes, you gain the following benefits: your Unarmed Strikes deal your choice of Acid, Cold, Fire, or Lightning damage instead of Bludgeoning; you can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of Unarmed Strikes; your reach increases by 10 feet when making Unarmed Strikes; Elemental Burst becomes available.

features.name: Elemental Burst
features.description: While Elemental Attunement is active, when you take the Attack action you can replace one attack with Elemental Burst: choose a 20-foot line or 20-foot cone originating from you. Each creature in the area must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your Monk save DC or take damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die plus your Wisdom modifier (same damage type as your attunement). Half on a success.

features.name: Environmental Burst
features.description: While Elemental Attunement is active, you can cast Elementalism as a Magic action without spending a spell slot or Focus Point. Additionally, when you use Elemental Burst, you can increase the area to a 30-foot line or 30-foot cone.

features.name: Stride of the Elements
features.description: While Elemental Attunement is active, you gain a Fly Speed and Swim Speed equal to your Speed.

features.name: Elemental Epitome
features.description: While Elemental Attunement is active, you also gain the following benefits: resistance to Acid, Cold, Fire, and Lightning damage; when you use your Elemental Burst, you can spend 1 Focus Point to make it strike all creatures in a 20-foot radius sphere centered on a point within 120 feet of you instead; when you use Deflect Attacks and succeed, you can spend 1 Focus Point to teleport the deflected attack's energy to a target you can see within 60 feet.

subclasses.name: Warrior of the Open Hand
subclasses.tagline: Master Unarmed Combat Techniques
subclasses.description: Warriors of the Open Hand are masters of unarmed combat. They learn techniques to push and trip their opponents and manipulate their own energy to protect themselves from harm.

3.name: Open Hand Technique
3.text: Whenever you hit a creature with an attack granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can impose one of the following effects on that target. Addle: the target can't make Opportunity Attacks until the start of its next turn. Push: the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 15 feet away from you. Topple: the target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the Prone condition.

6.name: Wholeness of Body
6.text: As a Bonus Action, you can roll your Martial Arts die and regain a number of Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1 Hit Point regained). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), regaining all uses on a Long Rest.

actions.name: Wholeness of Body
actions.effect: Regain Martial Arts die + WIS modifier HP

11.name: Fleet Step
11.text: When you take a Bonus Action other than Step of the Wind, you can also use Step of the Wind immediately after that Bonus Action.

17.name: Quivering Palm
17.text: When you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, you can expend 4 Focus Points to start imperceptible lethal vibrations in its body, lasting a number of days equal to your Monk level. The vibrations are harmless unless you take an action to end them (or forgo an attack during the Attack action). To end them, you and the target must be on the same plane of existence; the target must then make a Constitution saving throw, taking 10d12 Force damage on a failed save or half as much on a success. You can have only one creature under this effect at a time.

actions.name: Quivering Palm
actions.effect: Expend 4 Focus Points on a hit; later end the vibrations for CON save / 10d12 Force damage

features.name: Open Hand Technique
features.description: Whenever you hit a creature with one of the attacks granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can impose one of the following effects: Addle (the target can't make Opportunity Attacks until the start of its next turn), Push (the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 15 feet away from you), Topple (the target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the Prone condition).

features.name: Wholeness of Body
features.description: You gain the ability to heal yourself. As a Bonus Action, you can roll your Martial Arts die. You regain a number of Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1 Hit Point). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Fleet Step
features.description: When you take a Bonus Action other than Step of the Wind, you can also use Step of the Wind as part of that Bonus Action.

features.name: Quivering Palm
features.description: You gain the ability to set up lethal vibrations in someone's body. When you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, you can spend 4 Focus Points to start these imperceptible vibrations, which last for a number of days equal to your Monk level. The vibrations are harmless unless you use your action to end them. To do so, you and the target must be on the same plane of existence. When you use this action, the creature must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is reduced to 0 Hit Points. On a successful save, the creature takes 10d10 Necrotic damage. You can have only one creature under the effect of this feature at a time.

subclasses.name: Way of the Drunken Master
subclasses.edition_note: Originally published for 2014 rules in Xanathar's Guide to Everything; feature levels (3/6/11/17) are as printed in that book.
subclasses.tagline: Move with the Unpredictable Sway of a Drunkard
subclasses.description: The Way of the Drunken Master teaches its students to move with the jerky, unpredictable movements of a drunkard. The drunken master's erratic stumbles conceal a carefully executed dance of blocks, parries, advances, attacks, and retreats.

3.name: Bonus Proficiencies
3.text: When you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Performance skill if you don't already have it. You also gain proficiency with brewer's supplies if you don't already have it.

3.name: Drunken Technique
3.text: You learn how to twist and turn quickly as part of your Flurry of Blows. Whenever you use Flurry of Blows, you gain the benefit of the Disengage action, and your walking speed increases by 10 feet until the end of the current turn.

6.name: Tipsy Sway
6.text: You can move in sudden, swaying ways. You gain the following benefits. Leap to Your Feet: When you're prone, you can stand up by spending 5 feet of movement, rather than half your speed. Redirect Attack: When a creature misses you with a melee attack roll, you can spend 1 ki point as a reaction to cause that attack to hit one creature of your choice, other than the attacker, that you can see within 5 feet of you.

11.name: Drunkard's Luck
11.text: You always seem to get a lucky bounce at the right moment. When you make an ability check, an attack roll, or a saving throw and have disadvantage on the roll, you can spend 2 ki points to cancel the disadvantage for that roll.

17.name: Intoxicated Frenzy
17.text: You gain the ability to make an overwhelming number of attacks against a group of enemies. When you use your Flurry of Blows, you can make up to three additional attacks with it (up to a total of five Flurry of Blows attacks), provided that each Flurry of Blows attack targets a different creature this turn.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency in the Performance skill if you don't already have it. Your martial arts technique mixes combat training with the precision of a dancer and the antics of a jokester. You also gain proficiency with brewer's supplies if you don't already have it.

features.name: Drunken Technique
features.description: When you use Flurry of Blows, you can take the Disengage action as a Bonus Action, and your walking speed increases by 10 feet until the end of the current turn.

features.name: Tipsy Sway
features.description: You can move in sudden, swaying ways. You gain two benefits: Leap to Your Feet (when you're Prone, you can stand up by spending 5 feet of movement, rather than half your speed), Redirect Attack (when a creature misses you with a melee attack, you can spend 1 Focus Point and use your Reaction to cause that attack to hit one creature of your choice, other than the attacker, that you can see within 5 feet of you).

features.name: Drunkard's Luck
features.description: You always seem to get a lucky bounce at the right moment. When you make an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw and have disadvantage on the roll, you can spend 2 Focus Points to cancel the disadvantage for that roll.

features.name: Intoxicated Frenzy
features.description: You gain the ability to make an overwhelming number of attacks against a group of enemies. When you use Flurry of Blows, you can make up to three additional attacks with it (up to a total of five Flurry of Blows attacks), provided that each Flurry of Blows attack targets a different creature this turn.

subclasses.name: Way of the Kensei
subclasses.edition_note: Originally published for 2014 rules in Xanathar's Guide to Everything; feature levels (3/6/11/17) are as printed in that book.
subclasses.tagline: Make a Weapon an Extension of the Body
subclasses.description: Monks of the Way of the Kensei train relentlessly with their weapons, to the point where the weapon becomes an extension of the body. A kensei views a weapon as a tool used to express the beauty and precision of the martial arts.

3.name: Path of the Kensei
3.text: Your special martial arts training leads you to master the use of certain weapons. This path also includes instruction in the deft strokes of calligraphy or painting. Kensei Weapons: Choose two types of weapons to be your kensei weapons: one melee weapon and one ranged weapon. Each can be any simple or martial weapon that lacks the heavy and special properties; the longbow is also a valid choice. You gain proficiency with these weapons if you don't already have it, and they count as monk weapons for you. You add a weapon when you reach 6th, 11th, and 17th level in this class (gaining only one weapon at 17th). Whenever you choose a kensei weapon, it can be one you already have. You gain the following benefits while using kensei weapons. Agile Parry: If you make an unarmed strike as part of the Attack action on your turn and are holding a kensei weapon, you can use it to defend yourself if it is a melee weapon; you gain a +2 bonus to AC until the start of your next turn, while the weapon is in your hand and you aren't incapacitated. Kensei's Shot: You can use a bonus action on your turn to make your ranged attacks with a kensei weapon more deadly; when you do so, any target you hit with a ranged attack using a kensei weapon takes an extra 1d4 damage of the weapon's type. You retain this benefit until the end of the current turn. Way of the Brush: You gain proficiency with your choice of calligrapher's supplies or painter's supplies.

6.name: One with the Blade
6.text: You extend your ki into your kensei weapons, granting you the following benefits. Magic Kensei Weapons: Your attacks with your kensei weapons count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage. Deft Strike: When you hit a target with a kensei weapon, you can spend 1 ki point to cause the weapon to deal extra damage to the target equal to your Martial Arts die; you can use this feature only once on each of your turns.

11.name: Sharpen the Blade
11.text: You gain the ability to augment your weapons further with your ki. As a bonus action, you can expend up to 3 ki points to grant one kensei weapon you touch a bonus to attack and damage rolls when you attack with it; the bonus equals the number of ki points spent. This bonus lasts for 1 minute or until you use this feature again. This feature has no effect on a magic weapon that already has a bonus to attack and damage rolls.

17.name: Unerring Accuracy
17.text: Your mastery of weapons grants you extraordinary accuracy. If you miss with an attack roll using a monk weapon on your turn, you can reroll it. You can use this feature only once on each of your turns.

You can use these weapons as a Monk Weapon. You gain the following benefits with your kensei weapons: Agile Parry (if you make an unarmed strike as part of the Attack action and are holding a kensei melee weapon, you can use it to defend yourself — you gain +2 AC until the start of your next turn if you made an unarmed strike); Kensei's Shot (as a Bonus Action on your turn, you can make your ranged attacks more deadly — +1d4 damage on the next ranged attack); Way of the Brush (you gain proficiency with calligrapher's supplies or painter's supplies).

subclasses.name: Way of the Sun Soul
subclasses.edition_note: Originally published for 2014 rules in Xanathar's Guide to Everything; feature levels (3/6/11/17) are as printed in that book.
subclasses.tagline: Channel Life Energy into Searing Bolts of Light
subclasses.description: Monks of the Way of the Sun Soul learn to channel their life energy into searing bolts of light. They teach that meditation can unlock the ability to unleash the indomitable light shed by the soul of every living creature.

3.name: Radiant Sun Bolt
3.text: You can hurl searing bolts of magical radiance. You gain a new attack option that you can use with the Attack action. This special attack is a ranged spell attack with a range of 30 feet; you are proficient with it, and you add your Dexterity modifier to its attack and damage rolls. Its damage is radiant, and its damage die is a d4 (this die changes as you gain monk levels, as shown in the Martial Arts column of the Monk table). When you take the Attack action on your turn and use this special attack as part of it, you can spend 1 ki point to make the special attack twice as a bonus action.

actions.name: Radiant Sun Bolt
actions.effect: Ranged spell attack dealing Martial Arts die radiant damage

6.name: Searing Arc Strike
6.text: You gain the ability to channel your ki into searing waves of energy. Immediately after you take the Attack action on your turn, you can spend 2 ki points to cast the Burning Hands spell as a bonus action. You can spend additional ki points to cast Burning Hands as a higher-level spell; each additional ki point you spend increases the spell's level by 1. The maximum number of ki points (2 plus any additional points) that you can spend on the spell equals half your monk level.

11.name: Searing Sunburst
11.text: You gain the ability to create an orb of light that erupts into a devastating explosion. As an action, you magically create an orb and hurl it at a point you choose within 150 feet, where it erupts into a sphere of radiant light for a brief but deadly instant. Each creature in that 20-foot-radius sphere must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take 2d6 radiant damage (a creature doesn't need to make the save if it is behind total cover that is opaque). You can increase the sphere's damage by spending ki points; each point you spend, to a maximum of 3, increases the damage by 2d6.

17.name: Sun Shield
17.text: You become wreathed in a luminous, magical aura. You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet; you can extinguish or restore the light as a bonus action. If a creature hits you with a melee attack while this light shines, you can use your reaction to deal radiant damage to the creature; the radiant damage equals 5 + your Wisdom modifier.

This special attack is a ranged spell attack with a range of 30 feet and is proficient. It deals Radiant damage equal to 1d4 + your Dexterity modifier on a hit. When you make your Flurry of Blows attacks, you can replace each Unarmed Strike with this radiant bolt.

features.name: Implements of Mercy
features.description: You gain proficiency in the Insight and Medicine skills, and you gain proficiency with the herbalism kit.

features.name: Hand of Harm
features.description: Once per turn when you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike and spend a Focus Point for the attack, you can impose one of the following effects on that creature: the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or suffer the Poisoned condition until the end of your next turn; the target takes extra Necrotic damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die plus your Wisdom modifier.

features.name: Hand of Healing
features.description: As an action, you can spend 1 Focus Point to touch a creature and restore a number of hit points equal to a roll of your Martial Arts die + your Wisdom modifier. When you use your Flurry of Blows, you can replace one of the unarmed strikes with a use of this feature without spending a Focus Point for the healing.

features.name: Physician's Touch
features.description: You can administer even greater cures with a touch, and if you feel it's necessary, you can use your knowledge to cause harm. When you use Hand of Healing on a creature, you can also end one disease or one of the following conditions affecting the creature: Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, or Stunned. When you use Hand of Harm on a creature, you can subject that creature to the Stunned condition until the end of your next turn. A creature that succeeds on its saving throw isn't Stunned by this feature.

features.name: Flurry of Healing and Harm
features.description: You can now mete out a flurry of comfort and hurt. When you use Flurry of Blows, you can now replace each of the unarmed strikes with a use of your Hand of Healing, without spending Focus Points for the healing. In addition, when you make an Unarmed Strike with Flurry of Blows and the Hand of Harm effect, you can use that feature without spending a Focus Point.

features.name: Hand of Ultimate Mercy
features.description: Your mastery of life energy opens the door to the ultimate mercy. As an action, you can touch the corpse of a creature that died within the past 24 hours and expend 5 Focus Points. The creature then returns to life, regaining a number of hit points equal to 4d10 + your Wisdom modifier. If the creature died while subject to any of the following conditions, it revives with them removed: Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, and Stunned. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Arms of the Astral Self
features.description: Your mastery of your ki allows you to summon a portion of your astral self. As a Bonus Action, you can spend 1 Focus Point to summon the arms of your astral self. When you do so, each creature of your choice that you can see within 10 feet of you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take Force damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die. For 10 minutes, these spectral arms hover near your shoulders or surround your arms. You determine the arms' appearance, and they vanish early if you are incapacitated or die. While the spectral arms are present, you gain the following benefits: You can use your Wisdom modifier in place of your Strength modifier when making Strength checks and Strength saving throws; You can use the spectral arms to make unarmed strikes; When you make an unarmed strike with the arms on your turn, your reach for it is 5 feet greater than normal; The unarmed strikes with the arms count as your Martial Arts die on a hit.

features.name: Visage of the Astral Self
features.description: You can summon the visage of your astral self. As a Bonus Action, or as part of the Bonus Action you take to activate Arms of the Astral Self, you can spend 1 Focus Point to summon this visage for 10 minutes. It vanishes early if you are incapacitated or die. The spectral visage covers your face like a helmet or mask, and gives: Astral Sight (you can see normally in darkness, both magical and nonmagical, to a distance of 120 feet), Wisdom of the Spirit (you have Advantage on Wisdom and Charisma checks), Word of the Spirit (when you speak, you can direct your words to a creature of your choice that you can see within 60 feet of you, making it so only that creature can hear you. Alternatively, you can amplify your voice to be heard up to 600 feet away).

features.name: Body of the Astral Self
features.description: When you have both your astral arms and visage summoned, you can cause the body of your astral self to appear (no action required). This spectral body covers your physical form like a suit of armor, connecting your astral arms and visage. You determine its appearance. While the body is present, you gain the following benefits: Deflect Energy (when you take Acid, Cold, Fire, Force, Lightning, or Thunder damage, you can use your Reaction to deflect it; roll your Martial Arts die twice and reduce the damage by the total); Empowered Arms (once on each of your turns, when you hit a target with the Arms of the Astral Self, you can deal extra damage to the target equal to your Martial Arts die).

features.name: Awakened Astral Self
features.description: Your connection to your astral self is complete, allowing you to unleash its full potential. As a Bonus Action, you can spend 5 Focus Points to unleash the awakened astral self for 10 minutes. While your awakened astral self is active, you gain the following benefits: Armor of the Spirit (you gain a +2 bonus to Armor Class), Astral Barrage (whenever you use the Extra Attack feature to attack twice, you can instead attack three times if all three attacks are made with your astral arms).

You have a pool of healing power that replenishes when you finish a Long Rest; with that pool you can restore a total number of Hit Points equal to five times your Paladin level. As a Bonus Action, you can touch a creature (which could be yourself) and draw power from the pool to restore Hit Points, up to the maximum remaining. You can also expend 5 Hit Points from the pool to remove the Poisoned condition from the creature (those points don't also restore HP).

3.text: You can channel divine energy directly from the Outer Planes to fuel magical effects. You start with one effect: Divine Sense. Other Paladin features and your subclass give additional Channel Divinity options. You can use Channel Divinity twice; you regain one expended use on a Short Rest and all on a Long Rest, plus an additional use at Paladin level 11. If a Channel Divinity effect requires a save, the DC equals your Paladin spell save DC. Divine Sense: as a Bonus Action, you open your awareness to detect Celestials, Fiends, and Undead; for 10 minutes (or until Incapacitated) you know the location and creature type of any such creature within 60 feet, and you detect any consecrated or desecrated place or object within that radius.

It isn't enough for these paladins to establish order - they must crush the forces of chaos. Sometimes called knight tyrants or iron mongers, those who swear this oath gather into grim orders that serve gods or philosophies of war and well-ordered might.

Paladins who dedicate themselves to this oath believe that any person can be redeemed and that the path of benevolence and justice is one that anyone can walk. These paladins are known as redeemers.

actions.effect: Gain 1d8 + Wisdom modifier Temporary Hit Points

11.name: Subclass Feature
11.text: You gain a feature from your Ranger subclass.
11.description: You gain a feature from your Ranger subclass.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
12.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see chapter 5) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Ranger levels 16.
12.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

13.name: Relentless Hunter
13.text: Taking damage can't break your Concentration on Hunter's Mark.

14.name: Nature's Veil
14.text: You invoke spirits of nature to magically hide yourself. As a Bonus Action, you can give yourself the Invisible condition until the end of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

choices.label: Nature's Veil uses (= Wisdom modifier, min 1)

actions.name: Nature's Veil
actions.effect: Gain the Invisible condition until the end of your next turn

15.name: Subclass Feature
15.text: You gain a feature from your Ranger subclass.
15.description: You gain a feature from your Ranger subclass.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
16.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see chapter 5) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Ranger levels (this is the final Ranger Ability Score Improvement).
16.description: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

17.name: Precise Hunter
17.text: You have Advantage on attack rolls against the creature currently marked by your Hunter's Mark.

18.name: Feral Senses
18.text: Your connection to the forces of nature grants you Blindsight with a range of 30 feet.

19.name: Epic Boon
19.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see chapter 5) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Dimensional Travel is recommended.
19.description: You gain the Epic Boon of Truesight feat or another Epic Boon feat of your choice.

20.name: Foe Slayer
20.text: The damage die of your Hunter's Mark is a d10 rather than a d6.
20.description: Your Hunter's Mark now also deals extra damage equal to your Wisdom modifier whenever you hit the marked target, provided the spell is active on you.

subclasses.name: Beast Master
subclasses.tagline: Bond with a Primal Beast
subclasses.description: A Beast Master forms a mystical bond with a special animal, drawing on primal magic and a deep connection to the natural world.

3.name: Primal Companion
3.text: You magically summon a primal beast, which draws strength from your bond with nature. Choose its stat block: Beast of the Land, Beast of the Sea, or Beast of the Sky. You also determine the kind of animal it is, choosing a kind appropriate for the stat block. The beast is Friendly to you and your allies and obeys your commands; it vanishes if you die. In combat the beast acts during your turn: it can move and use its Reaction on its own, but the only action it takes is the Dodge action unless you take a Bonus Action to command it to take an action in its stat block or some other action. You can also sacrifice one of your attacks when you take the Attack action to command the beast to take the Beast's Strike action. If you have the Incapacitated condition, the beast acts on its own and isn't limited to the Dodge action. If the beast has died within the last hour, you can take a Magic action to touch it and expend a spell slot; the beast returns to life after 1 minute with all its Hit Points restored. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can summon a different primal beast (it appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you; the old one vanishes).

options.detail: Medium Beast. AC 13 + your Wisdom modifier. HP 5 plus five times your Ranger level (Hit Dice d8 = Ranger level). Speed 40 ft., Climb 40 ft. STR 14, DEX 14, CON 15, INT 8, WIS 14, CHA 11. Senses Darkvision 60 ft. Traits: Primal Bond (add your Proficiency Bonus to any ability check or saving throw the beast makes). Beast's Strike (Melee Attack Roll, bonus = your spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft.): 1d8 + 2 plus your Wisdom modifier Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage (your choice when summoned); if the beast moved at least 20 feet straight toward the target before the hit, the target takes an extra 1d6 damage of the same type and has the Prone condition if Large or smaller.

Medium Beast. AC 13 + your Wisdom modifier. HP 5 plus five times your Ranger level (Hit Dice d8 = Ranger level). Speed 5 ft., Swim 60 ft. STR 14, DEX 14, CON 15, INT 8, WIS 14, CHA 11. Senses Darkvision 90 ft. Traits: Amphibious (breathe air and water); Primal Bond. Beast's Strike (Melee Attack Roll, bonus = your spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft.): 1d6 + 2 plus your Wisdom modifier Bludgeoning or Piercing damage (your choice when summoned), and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC equals your spell save DC).

Small Beast. AC 13 + your Wisdom modifier. HP 4 plus four times your Ranger level (Hit Dice d6 = Ranger level). Speed 10 ft., Fly 60 ft. STR 6, DEX 16, CON 13, INT 8, WIS 14, CHA 11. Senses Darkvision 60 ft. Traits: Flyby (doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks when flying out of an enemy's reach); Primal Bond. Beast's Strike (Melee Attack Roll, bonus = your spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft.): 1d4 + 3 plus your Wisdom modifier Slashing damage.

actions.name: Command Primal Companion
actions.effect: Command the beast to take an action in its stat block or another action

7.name: Exceptional Training
7.text: When you take a Bonus Action to command your Primal Companion beast to take an action, you can also command it to take the Dash, Disengage, Dodge, or Help action using its Bonus Action. In addition, whenever it hits with an attack roll and deals damage, it can deal your choice of Force damage or its normal damage type.

11.name: Bestial Fury
11.text: When you command your Primal Companion beast to take the Beast's Strike action, the beast can use it twice. In addition, the first time each turn it hits a creature under the effect of your Hunter's Mark spell, the beast deals extra Force damage equal to the bonus damage of that spell.

15.name: Share Spells
15.text: When you cast a spell targeting yourself, you can also affect your Primal Companion beast with the spell if the beast is within 30 feet of you.

features.name: Primal Companion
features.description: You magically summon a primal beast, which draws from the magical energy of the natural world. Choose Beast of the Land, Beast of the Sea, or Beast of the Sky. The beast obeys your commands and uses your proficiency bonus. It acts on your initiative, taking its turn immediately after yours. It can move and use its reaction on its own, but the only action it takes is the Dodge action unless you take a Bonus Action to command it. In combat you can use your Bonus Action to command the beast to take any action in its stat block or the Dash, Disengage, Help, Hide, or Search action. When the beast drops to 0 HP, it disappears and you can resummon it after a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Exceptional Training
features.description: On any of your turns when your beast companion doesn't attack, you can use a Bonus Action to command the beast to take the Dash, Disengage, Dodge, or Help action. In addition, the beast's attacks now count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

features.name: Bestial Fury
features.description: When you command your beast companion to take the Attack action, the beast can make two attacks, or it can take the Multiattack action if it has that action.

features.name: Share Spells
features.description: When you cast a spell targeting yourself, you can also affect your beast companion with the spell if the beast is within 30 feet of you.

subclasses.name: Fey Wanderer
subclasses.tagline: Wield Fey Mirth and Fury
subclasses.description: A fey mystique surrounds you, thanks to the boon of an archfey or a location in the Feywild that transformed you. Your joyful laughter brightens the hearts of the downtrodden, and your martial prowess strikes terror in your foes.

3.name: Dreadful Strikes
3.text: You can augment your weapon strikes with mind-scarring magic drawn from the murky hollows of the Feywild. When you hit a creature with a weapon, you can deal an extra 1d4 Psychic damage to the target, which can take this extra damage only once per turn. The extra damage increases to 1d6 when you reach Ranger level 11.

3.name: Fey Wanderer Spells
3.text: When you reach a Ranger level specified in the table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. These don't count against the number of spells you can prepare.

3.name: Otherworldly Glamour
3.text: Whenever you make a Charisma check, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1). You also gain proficiency in one of these skills of your choice: Deception, Performance, or Persuasion. You also possess a fey blessing chosen from the Feywild Gifts table (or determined randomly).

options.value: Illusory butterflies flutter around you while you take a Short or Long Rest.
Flowers bloom from your hair each dawn.
You faintly smell of cinnamon, lavender, nutmeg, or another comforting herb or spice.
Your shadow dances while no one is looking directly at it.
Horns or antlers sprout from your head.
Your skin and hair change color each dawn.

7.name: Beguiling Twist
7.text: The magic of the Feywild guards your mind. You have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Charmed or Frightened condition. In addition, whenever you or a creature you can see within 120 feet of you succeeds on a saving throw to avoid or end the Charmed or Frightened condition, you can take a Reaction to force a different creature you can see within 120 feet of yourself to make a Wisdom save against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target is Charmed or Frightened (your choice) for 1 minute; the target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

11.name: Fey Reinforcements
11.text: You can cast Summon Fey without a Material component. You can also cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a Long Rest. Whenever you start casting the spell, you can modify it so that it doesn't require Concentration; if you do so, the spell's duration becomes 1 minute for that casting.

15.name: Misty Wanderer
15.text: You can cast Misty Step without expending a spell slot. You can do so a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. In addition, whenever you cast Misty Step, you can bring along one willing creature you can see within 5 feet of yourself; that creature teleports to an unoccupied space of your choice within 5 feet of your destination space.

features.name: Fey Wanderer Spells
features.description: You always have the following spells prepared: 3rd (Charm Person), 5th (Misty Step), 9th (Dispel Magic), 13th (Dimension Door), 17th (Mislead).

features.name: Dreadful Strikes
features.description: You can augment your weapon strikes with mind-scarring magic drawn from the murky Feywild. When you hit a creature with a weapon, you can deal an extra 1d4 Psychic damage to the target, which can take this extra damage only once per turn. The extra damage increases to 1d6 when you reach 11th level in this class.

features.name: Otherworldly Glamour
features.description: Your fey qualities give you a supernatural charm. As a result, you gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Deception, Performance, or Persuasion. In addition, whenever you make a Charisma check, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1).

features.name: Beguiling Twist
features.description: The magic of the Feywild guards your mind. You have advantage on saving throws against being Charmed or Frightened. In addition, whenever you or a creature you can see within 120 feet of you succeeds on a saving throw against being Charmed or Frightened, you can use your reaction to force a different creature you can see within 120 feet to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. If the save fails, the target is Charmed or Frightened by you (your choice) for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

features.name: Fey Reinforcements
features.description: The royal courts of the Feywild have blessed you with the assistance of fey beings: you know Summon Fey. It doesn't count against the number of Ranger spells you know and you can cast it without a material component. You can also cast it once without a spell slot, regaining the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Misty Wanderer
features.description: You can slip in and out of the Feywild to move in a blink of an eye. You can cast Misty Step without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. In addition, whenever you cast Misty Step, you can bring along one willing creature you can see within 5 feet of you. That creature teleports to an unoccupied space of your choice within 5 feet of your destination space.

subclasses.name: Gloom Stalker
subclasses.tagline: Draw on Shadow Magic to Fight Your Foes
subclasses.description: Gloom Stalkers are at home in the darkest places, wielding magic drawn from the Shadowfell to combat enemies that lurk in darkness.

3.name: Dread Ambusher
3.text: You have mastered the art of creating fearsome ambushes, granting you the following benefits. Ambusher's Leap: At the start of your first turn of each combat, your Speed increases by 10 feet until the end of that turn. Dreadful Strike: When you attack a creature and hit it with a weapon, you can deal an extra 2d6 Psychic damage; you can use this benefit only once per turn, a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. Initiative Bonus: When you roll Initiative, you can add your Wisdom modifier to the roll.

choices.label: Dreadful Strike uses (= Wisdom modifier, min 1)

3.name: Gloom Stalker Spells
3.text: When you reach a Ranger level specified in the table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. These don't count against the number of spells you can prepare.

3.name: Umbral Sight
3.text: You gain Darkvision with a range of 60 feet. If you already have Darkvision when you gain this feature, its range increases by 60 feet. You are also adept at evading creatures that rely on Darkvision: while entirely in Darkness, you have the Invisible condition to any creature that relies on Darkvision to see you in that Darkness.

7.name: Iron Mind
7.text: You have honed your ability to resist mind-altering powers. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws. If you already have this proficiency, you instead gain proficiency in Intelligence or Charisma saving throws (your choice).

choices.label: Saving throw proficiency (only if you already have Wisdom save proficiency)

11.name: Stalker's Flurry
11.text: The Psychic damage of your Dreadful Strike becomes 2d8. In addition, when you use the Dreadful Strike effect of your Dread Ambusher feature, you can cause one of the following additional effects. Sudden Strike: You can make another attack with the same weapon against a different creature that is within 5 feet of the original target and within the weapon's range. Mass Fear: The target and each creature within 10 feet of it must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC; on a failed save, a creature has the Frightened condition until the start of your next turn.

15.name: Shadowy Dodge
15.text: When a creature makes an attack roll against you, you can take a Reaction to impose Disadvantage on that roll. Whether the attack hits or misses, you can then teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

features.name: Gloom Stalker Spells
features.description: You always have the following spells prepared: 3rd (Disguise Self, Rope Trick), 5th (Ambush, Rope Trick), 9th (Fear, Rope Trick), 13th (Greater Invisibility, Rope Trick), 17th (Seeming, Rope Trick). Note: exact spells are Disguise Self (3rd), Rope Trick (3rd), Fear (5th), Greater Invisibility (7th), Seeming (9th).

features.name: Dread Ambusher
features.description: You master the art of the ambush. You can give yourself a bonus to your Initiative rolls equal to your Wisdom modifier. At the start of your first turn of each combat, your walking speed increases by 10 feet, which lasts until the end of that turn. If you take the Attack action on that turn, you can make one additional weapon attack as part of that action. If that attack hits, the target takes an extra 1d8 damage of the weapon's damage type.

features.name: Umbral Sight
features.description: You gain Darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision from your race, its range increases by 30 feet. You are also adept at evading creatures that rely on darkvision. While in darkness, you are invisible to any creature that relies on darkvision to see you in that darkness.

features.name: Iron Mind
features.description: You have honed your ability to resist the mind-altering powers of your prey. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency in Intelligence or Charisma saving throws (your choice).

features.name: Stalker's Flurry
features.description: You learn to attack with such unexpected speed that you can turn a miss into another strike. Once on each of your turns when you miss with a weapon attack, you can make another weapon attack as part of the same action.

features.name: Shadowy Dodge
features.description: You can dodge in unforeseen ways, with wisps of supernatural shadow around you. Whenever a creature makes an attack roll against you and doesn't have advantage on the roll, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on it. You must use this feature before you know the outcome of the attack roll.

subclasses.name: Hunter
subclasses.tagline: Protect Nature and People from Destruction
subclasses.description: You stalk prey in the wilds and elsewhere, using your abilities as a Hunter to protect nature and people everywhere from forces that would destroy them.

3.name: Hunter's Lore
3.text: You can call on the forces of nature to reveal certain strengths and weaknesses of your prey. While a creature is marked by your Hunter's Mark, you know whether that creature has any Immunities, Resistances, or Vulnerabilities, and if the creature has any, you know what they are.

3.name: Hunter's Prey
3.text: You gain one of the following feature options of your choice. Whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest, you can replace the chosen option with the other one.

options.detail: Your tenacity can wear down even the most resilient foes. When you hit a creature with a weapon, the weapon deals an extra 1d8 damage to the target if it's missing any of its Hit Points. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn.

Once on each of your turns when you make an attack with a weapon, you can make another attack with the same weapon against a different creature that is within 5 feet of the original target, within the weapon's range, and that you haven't attacked this turn.

7.name: Defensive Tactics
7.text: You gain one of the following feature options of your choice. Whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest, you can replace the chosen option with the other one.

options.detail: Opportunity Attacks have Disadvantage against you.
When a creature hits you with an attack roll, that creature has Disadvantage on all other attack rolls against you this turn.

11.name: Superior Hunter's Prey
11.text: Once per turn when you deal damage to a creature marked by your Hunter's Mark, you can also deal that spell's extra damage to a different creature that you can see within 30 feet of the first creature.

15.name: Superior Hunter's Defense
15.text: When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to give yourself Resistance to that damage and any other damage of the same type until the end of the current turn.

features.name: Hunter's Prey
features.description: You gain one of the following features of your choice: Colossus Slayer (once per turn when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, the creature takes 1d8 extra damage if it's below its hit point maximum); Giant Killer (when a Large or larger creature within 5 feet makes an attack against a creature other than you, you can use your reaction to attack that creature); Horde Breaker (once on each of your turns, when you make a weapon attack, you can make another attack with the same weapon against a different creature within 5 feet of the original target and within range).

features.name: Defensive Tactics
features.description: You gain one of the following features of your choice: Escape the Horde (opportunity attacks against you are made with disadvantage); Multiattack Defense (when a creature hits you with an attack, you gain +4 bonus to AC against all subsequent attacks made by that creature for the rest of the turn); Steel Will (you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened).

features.name: Multiattack
features.description: You gain one of the following features of your choice: Volley (you can use your action to make a ranged attack against any number of creatures within 10 feet of a point you can see within your weapon's range, using a separate attack roll for each target; you must have ammunition for each, and you don't add your ability modifier to the damage roll unless it is negative); Whirlwind Attack (you can use your action to make a melee attack against any number of creatures within 5 feet of you, using a separate attack roll for each target).

features.name: Superior Hunter's Defense
features.description: You gain one of the following features of your choice: Evasion (when subjected to an effect that allows a Dexterity saving throw for half damage, you take no damage on a success and half on a failure); Stand Against the Tide (when a hostile creature misses you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to force that creature to repeat the same attack against another creature of your choice); Uncanny Dodge (when an attacker you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage).

subclasses.name: Horizon Walker
subclasses.edition_note: Originally published for 2014 rules in Xanathar's Guide to Everything; feature levels are as printed in that book.
subclasses.tagline: Guard the World Against Planar Threats
subclasses.description: Horizon Walkers guard the world against threats that originate from other planes or that seek to ravage the mortal realm with otherworldly magic. They seek out planar portals and keep watch over them.

3.name: Horizon Walker Magic
3.text: You learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class. The spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of ranger spells you know. Ranger level 3: Protection from Evil and Good. Level 5: Misty Step. Level 9: Haste. Level 13: Banishment. Level 17: Teleportation Circle.

3.name: Detect Portal
3.text: You gain the ability to magically sense the presence of a planar portal. As an action, you detect the distance and direction to the closest planar portal within 1 mile of you. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

3.name: Planar Warrior
3.text: You learn to draw on the energy of the multiverse to augment your attacks. As a bonus action, choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The next time you hit that creature on this turn with a weapon attack, all damage dealt by the attack becomes force damage, and the creature takes an extra 1d8 force damage from the attack. When you reach 11th level in this class, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

actions.name: Planar Warrior
actions.effect: Mark a creature; your next hit deals force damage + 1d8 (2d8 at 11th)

7.name: Ethereal Step
7.text: You learn to step through the Ethereal Plane. As a bonus action, you can cast the Etherealness spell with this feature, without expending a spell slot, but the spell ends at the end of the current turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

11.name: Distant Strike
11.text: You gain the ability to pass between the planes in the blink of an eye. When you take the Attack action, you can teleport up to 10 feet before each attack to an unoccupied space you can see. If you attack at least two different creatures with the action, you can make one additional attack with it against a third creature.

15.name: Spectral Defense
15.text: Your ability to move between planes enables you to slip through the planar boundaries to lessen the harm done to you during battle. When you take damage from an attack, you can use your reaction to give yourself resistance to all of that attack's damage on this turn.

features.name: Horizon Walker Spells
features.description: You always have the following spells prepared: 3rd (Protection from Evil and Good), 5th (Misty Step), 9th (Haste), 13th (Banishment), 17th (Teleportation Circle).

features.name: Detect Portal

subclasses.name: Monster Slayer
subclasses.edition_note: Originally published for 2014 rules in Xanathar's Guide to Everything; feature levels are as printed in that book.
subclasses.tagline: Hunt Creatures of the Night and Wielders of Grim Magic
subclasses.description: You have dedicated yourself to hunting down creatures of the night and wielders of grim magic. A Monster Slayer seeks out vampires, dragons, evil fey, fiends, and other magical threats, trained in supernatural techniques to overcome such monsters.

3.name: Monster Slayer Magic
3.text: You learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class. The spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of ranger spells you know. Ranger level 3: Protection from Evil and Good. Level 5: Zone of Truth. Level 9: Magic Circle. Level 13: Banishment. Level 17: Hold Monster.

3.name: Hunter's Sense
3.text: You gain the ability to peer at a creature and magically discern how best to hurt it. As an action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. You immediately learn whether the creature has any damage immunities, resistances, or vulnerabilities and what they are; if the creature is hidden from divination magic, you sense that it has no damage immunities, resistances, or vulnerabilities. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

choices.label: Hunter's Sense uses (= Wisdom modifier, min 1)

3.name: Slayer's Prey
3.text: You can focus your ire on one foe, increasing the harm you inflict on it. As a bonus action, you designate one creature you can see within 60 feet of you as the target of this feature. The first time each turn that you hit that target with a weapon attack, it takes an extra 1d6 damage from the weapon. This benefit lasts until you finish a short or long rest; it ends early if you designate a different creature.

actions.name: Slayer's Prey
actions.effect: Designate a target; first hit each turn deals +1d6 damage

7.name: Supernatural Defense
7.text: You gain extra resilience against your prey's assaults on your mind and body. Whenever the target of your Slayer's Prey forces you to make a saving throw, and whenever you make an ability check to escape that target's grapple, add 1d6 to your roll.

11.name: Magic-User's Nemesis
11.text: You gain the ability to thwart someone else's magic. When you see a creature casting a spell or teleporting within 60 feet of you, you can use your reaction to try to magically foil it. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, or its spell or teleport fails and is wasted. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

15.name: Slayer's Counter
15.text: You gain the ability to counterattack when your prey tries to sabotage you. If the target of your Slayer's Prey forces you to make a saving throw, you can use your reaction to make one weapon attack against the quarry. You make this attack immediately before making the saving throw; if your attack hits, your save automatically succeeds, in addition to the attack's normal effects.

If the target of your Slayer's Prey forces you to make a saving throw, you can use your reaction to make one weapon attack against the quarry. You make this attack immediately before making the saving throw. If the attack hits, your saving throw automatically succeeds, in addition to the attack's normal effects.

features.name: Gathered Swarm
features.description: A swarm of intangible nature spirits has bonded itself to you and can assist you in battle. Until you die, the swarm remains in your space, crawls all over you, and occasionally we slips into your clothing. Whenever you hit a creature with an attack roll, the swarm can assist in one of three ways: move the creature 15 ft in a direction of your choice; move you 5 ft in a direction of your choice; deal 1d6 piercing or slashing damage (your choice) to the target. The swarm type is chosen when you gain this feature (insects, birds, leaves, spirits, etc.).

features.name: Swarmkeeper Spells
features.description: 3rd: Faerie Fire, Mage Hand; 5th: Web; 9th: Gaseous Form; 13th: Arcane Eye; 17th: Insect Plague.

features.name: Writhing Tide
features.description: You can condense part of your swarm into a focused mass that lifts you up. As a Bonus Action, you gain a flying speed of 10 feet and can hover. This effect lasts for 1 minute. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Mighty Swarm
features.description: Your Gathered Swarm grows mightier in the following ways: the damage of Gathered Swarm increases to 1d8; if you move a creature, it is Grappled; if you move yourself, you gain Half Cover until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Swarming Dispersal
features.description: You can momentarily disperse your body into your swarm, avoiding danger. When you take damage, you can use your Reaction to give yourself Resistance to that damage. You vanish into your swarm and then re-emerge, and you can teleport to an unoccupied space that you can see within 30 feet of you. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

weapon_proficiencies: Martial weapons that have the Finesse or Light property

1.description: Choose two of your skill proficiencies. Your Proficiency Bonus is doubled for any ability check you make using either of the chosen proficiencies. At level 6, you choose two more of your proficiencies (in skills or with thieves' tools) to gain this benefit.

1.name: Sneak Attack
1.text: You know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack roll if you have Advantage on the roll and the attack uses a Finesse or a Ranged weapon. The extra damage's type is the same as the weapon's type. You don't need Advantage on the attack roll if at least one of your allies is within 5 feet of the target, the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition, and you don't have Disadvantage on the attack roll. The extra damage increases as you gain Rogue levels, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue Features table.

choices.label: Sneak Attack damage dice (d6; see progression_table)

1.description: Once per turn, you can deal extra damage to one creature you hit with an attack roll if you have Advantage on the roll and the attack uses a Finesse or a Ranged weapon.
